item.title: Bill Cowher calls for Browns to commit to Shedeur Sanders
item.description: Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images, CBS The Cleveland Browns have gotten off to a better start to the NFL season than anyone expected . The longtime basement dwellers of the league were 5–3 heading into Sunday’s showdown on the road against the New Orleans Saints. Cleveland had to make one significant change to the lineup before their game on Sunday, with backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders stepping up to start due to Deshaun Watson missing the week’s worth of practice while in the league’s concussion protocol. The Browns ultimately lost to the Saints 23–22 in overtime, but Sanders showed enough skill to have Browns fans excited for what could be in store for their young quarterback, and even convinced some analysts that it was time for Cleveland to embrace the future. Speaking after the game, former Steelers coach Bill Cowher was adamant that the Browns should commit to Sanders under center full time, even if Watson were to be available next week. “I would just say this: Moving forward, Shedeur Sanders should be the starter for this football team,” Cowher said. “He’s going to be the future. And I think what he showed today, his resilience, continued to come back. He made great decisions, he extended plays. I love the way he played and I would move forward with him.” When cohost Nate Burleson asked if Cowher believed Watson hadn’t played well enough to get his job back when healthy, Cowher said it was more important to look into the future. “One person’s unfortunate situation creates another person’s opportunity. I just think that right now, what I saw from Shedeur Sanders, I would move forward. Because he is the future of your football team.” “Shedeur Sanders should be the starter for this football team. He’s gonna be the future.” – Bill Cowher https://t.co/UN78KLHXxX — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 8, 2026 While it might sound odd for a team to consider starting its 0–1 backup quarterback over its 5–3 starting quarterback when both are healthy, the game that Sanders played on Sunday showed why it might be worth looking into for the Browns. Sanders finished the game 297 passing yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions. His QB rating was 114.6 on the day. In Watson’s eight starts this season, he’s cleared 270 yards passing just twice, thrown for two touchdowns just twice, and has never done both in the same game. Just one of his eight starts saw him record a QB rating in the triple digits. Further, Sanders was able to deliver in crunch time when the Browns needed him, creating space and throwing an impressive pass in the final minute to put his team in position to kick a game-tying field goal to force overtime. This play alone is better than anything Watson has done all year. Keep developing Shedeur. He’s the future. https://t.co/6udkhpSyqk — Brownies (@BrowniesToBowl) November 8, 2026 Beyond his play on the field, there’s plenty more extremely simple reasons the Browns might want to get a head start on the potential Sanders era.
item.content:encoded: Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images, CBS The Cleveland Browns have gotten off to a better start to the NFL season than anyone expected . The longtime basement dwellers of the league were 5–3 heading into Sunday’s showdown on the road against the New Orleans Saints. Cleveland had to make one significant change to the lineup before their game on Sunday, with backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders stepping up to start due to Deshaun Watson missing the week’s worth of practice while in the league’s concussion protocol. The Browns ultimately lost to the Saints 23–22 in overtime, but Sanders showed enough skill to have Browns fans excited for what could be in store for their young quarterback, and even convinced some analysts that it was time for Cleveland to embrace the future. Speaking after the game, former Steelers coach Bill Cowher was adamant that the Browns should commit to Sanders under center full time, even if Watson were to be available next week. “I would just say this: Moving forward, Shedeur Sanders should be the starter for this football team,” Cowher said. “He’s going to be the future. And I think what he showed today, his resilience, continued to come back. He made great decisions, he extended plays. I love the way he played and I would move forward with him.” When cohost Nate Burleson asked if Cowher believed Watson hadn’t played well enough to get his job back when healthy, Cowher said it was more important to look into the future. “One person’s unfortunate situation creates another person’s opportunity. I just think that right now, what I saw from Shedeur Sanders, I would move forward. Because he is the future of your football team.” “Shedeur Sanders should be the starter for this football team. He’s gonna be the future.” – Bill Cowher https://t.co/UN78KLHXxX — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 8, 2026 While it might sound odd for a team to consider starting its 0–1 backup quarterback over its 5–3 starting quarterback when both are healthy, the game that Sanders played on Sunday showed why it might be worth looking into for the Browns. Sanders finished the game 297 passing yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions. His QB rating was 114.6 on the day. In Watson’s eight starts this season, he’s cleared 270 yards passing just twice, thrown for two touchdowns just twice, and has never done both in the same game. Just one of his eight starts saw him record a QB rating in the triple digits. Further, Sanders was able to deliver in crunch time when the Browns needed him, creating space and throwing an impressive pass in the final minute to put his team in position to kick a game-tying field goal to force overtime. This play alone is better than anything Watson has done all year. Keep developing Shedeur. He’s the future. https://t.co/6udkhpSyqk — Brownies (@BrowniesToBowl) November 8, 2026 Beyond his play on the field, there’s plenty more extremely simple reasons the Browns might want to get a head start on the potential Sanders era. First and foremost, Watson is still the same guy that was accused of sexual misconduct by dozens of women before joining the Browns. His contract has also been an albatross since the moment it was signed, and will go down as one of the worst in NFL history. While the 5–3 start may have felt somewhat vindicating for the crowd that signed Watson to his ridiculous deal in the first place, the sooner the team can move on from it, the better. We’re still only a few months removed from Watson criticizing Browns fans for having the audacity to boo him . Further, it’s best for the Browns to figure out as soon as possible whether or not Sanders really is the team’s next franchise quarterback, or if they are going to have to go back to the draft to find another in the coming seasons. Giving him a shot now could go a long way towards finding an answer there, and thus giving the Browns a better idea of how to approach the coming offseason. The complicating factor here, at least to the Browns, may be the fact that for the first time in recent memory, their team doesn’t stink. With Watson holding a winning record and Sanders now 0–1, they might not be able to stomach giving the keys to the young player over the veteran when the move could backfire. That said, Watson has had literally four years to show he’s good enough to lead the Browns to victory, and has only started showing signs of such an ability this year and $200 million later. Whatever the Browns decide to do, for the first time in a long time, their decision might have a legitimate impact on the playoff picture across the league. item.title: 3 takeaways as Penn State overpowers Wisconsin volleyball in five sets
item.description: MADISON – For as many big wins as Wisconsin volleyball ’s youthful 2026 roster has pulled off, the Badgers (and their nine freshmen) met their match against a more experienced Penn State group. The seventh-ranked Badgers fell to No. 11 Penn State in five sets, 25-20, 18-25, 25-20, 19-25, 11-15, on Nov. 8 at the UW Field House. The Nittany Lions ’ upperclassmen had 54 kills against Wisconsin , which were three fewer than what the Badgers’ entire roster had. “That was a tough loss for us,” Wisconsin setter Charlie Fuerbringer said. “I know we wanted to win that bad. But I was really proud of how we battled and stuck together through the good times and the bad times.” Here are three takeaways from the loss: Wisconsin can’t stop Penn State star Kennedy Martin’s onslaught Penn State kept going to Kennedy Martin with its attack, and Wisconsin did not have any answers. Martin – a first-team All-American in each of the last two seasons – finished with 28 kills, coming up three short of tying the UW Field House record for an opposing player. She did so while taking 64 of Penn State’s 163 swings and hitting .328. “Errors don’t affect her,” Wisconsin coach Kelly Sheffield said. “They certainly don’t seem to affect her. She makes really good decisions. She can work the court. She doesn’t get blocked very much. She has great vision of seeing what is in front of her, and she’s a handful.” Wisconsin had its hands full trying to stop her from the beginning. She had nine kills in the first set and another six in the second set. Wisconsin’s win in the third set coincided with Martin’s one less-than-stellar set, as she had only two kills with one error on 11 swings. The Badgers join a long list of teams that have struggled to slow down Martin. The 6-foot-6 senior right-side hitter has now recorded at least 20 kills in five of her last seven matches. Even before the UW match, her 4.58 kills per set led the Big Ten. “She’s been an aircraft carrier for the teams that she’s been on, and she doesn’t flinch,” Sheffield said. item.content:encoded: MADISON – For as many big wins as Wisconsin volleyball ’s youthful 2026 roster has pulled off, the Badgers (and their nine freshmen) met their match against a more experienced Penn State group. The seventh-ranked Badgers fell to No. 11 Penn State in five sets, 25-20, 18-25, 25-20, 19-25, 11-15, on Nov. 8 at the UW Field House. The Nittany Lions ’ upperclassmen had 54 kills against Wisconsin , which were three fewer than what the Badgers’ entire roster had. “That was a tough loss for us,” Wisconsin setter Charlie Fuerbringer said. “I know we wanted to win that bad. But I was really proud of how we battled and stuck together through the good times and the bad times.” Here are three takeaways from the loss: Wisconsin can’t stop Penn State star Kennedy Martin’s onslaught Penn State kept going to Kennedy Martin with its attack, and Wisconsin did not have any answers. Martin – a first-team All-American in each of the last two seasons – finished with 28 kills, coming up three short of tying the UW Field House record for an opposing player. She did so while taking 64 of Penn State’s 163 swings and hitting .328. “Errors don’t affect her,” Wisconsin coach Kelly Sheffield said. “They certainly don’t seem to affect her. She makes really good decisions. She can work the court. She doesn’t get blocked very much. She has great vision of seeing what is in front of her, and she’s a handful.” Wisconsin had its hands full trying to stop her from the beginning. She had nine kills in the first set and another six in the second set. Wisconsin’s win in the third set coincided with Martin’s one less-than-stellar set, as she had only two kills with one error on 11 swings. The Badgers join a long list of teams that have struggled to slow down Martin. The 6-foot-6 senior right-side hitter has now recorded at least 20 kills in five of her last seven matches. Even before the UW match, her 4.58 kills per set led the Big Ten. “She’s been an aircraft carrier for the teams that she’s been on, and she doesn’t flinch,” Sheffield said. Martin’s constant threat opened up opportunities for others. Whitney Lauenstein had 15 kills, Kendall Northern had nine kills, Gabrielle Nichols had eight kills and Emmi Sellman had seven kills. Northern, Nichols and Stucky each hit .375 or better. Penn State’s serves keep Wisconsin out of system Penn State’s serves posed a major challenge for Wisconsin. It was most obvious when the Nittany Lions aced the Badgers on three consecutive points in the fourth set. It was while outside hitters Audrey Flanagan and Eva Travis were with libero Anna Bardaro in the back row. Sheffield called a timeout after the second ace, only for Martin to ace the Badgers for a third time – more than against any other ranked opponent this season. Sheffield then subbed Grace Egan into the back row before the service run finally ended. “Our outsides had a tough time handling their serves, no doubt,” Sheffield said. “It stressed our patterns. They’ve got some servers that can really get at it. But yeah, there was some times we got broken down a little bit.” Those aces turned Wisconsin’s 7-5 deficit into a more glaring 10-5 deficit in the fourth set. The Badgers later cut it to 20-18 before the Nittany Lions went on a 5-1 run to finish off the set (and take the momentum ahead of the fifth set). Penn State had two other aces in the match, but that hardly scratches the surface of the serving impact. Good serves – ace or otherwise – helped the Nittany Lions go on 5-0 and 4-0 runs in the second set, a 4-0 run in the third set and a 6-1 run in the fifth set. The Badgers sided out only 54%, 45% and 53% of the time, respectively, in the second, fourth and fifth sets – the three that they lost. Penn State, on the other hand, sided out 73%, 60% and 72% of the time in those three sets. “When we were out of system, we couldn’t execute,” Fuerbringer said. “We weren’t sticking with the play as well as they were. … When they would be out of system, they would go up and all of their players would be covering maybe once or twice more than what we were doing.” Decelise Champion overcomes slow start After committing a season-high 12 attack errors against Michigan State, Decelise Champion struggled early against Penn State as well. Champion had only one kill versus three attack errors in the first set, resulting in a minus-.400 hitting percentage. It was a noticeable contrast from her team-high average of 3.8 kills per set in 2026. The 17-year-old opposite hitter also had relatively quiet second, fourth and fifth sets, picking up a combined eight kills versus five attack errors. But she was a key part of the Badgers’ win in the third set. Champion had 10 kills on 13 total attacks without any errors in the set. She delivered four of those kills during the Badgers’ 7-2 run to finish off the set. Champion ultimately finished with 19 kills and eight attack errors while hitting .220. She took 50 of UW’s 135 swings. “It was definitely challenging,” Champion said. “I felt like these past two matches, I’ve had a slow start in my attacking and how I’m approaching the court. … Overall, it was a really big challenge for the team and for everyone. So like Charlie said, we’re going to learn a lot from this.” This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: 3 takeaways as Penn State overpowers Wisconsin volleyball in five sets

item.title: Patriots QB Drake Maye’s brutally honest self-assessment after Packers loss is on point
item.description: Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images Patriots QB Drake Maye’s brutally honest self-assessment after Packers loss is on point appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots lost 45-27 at Gillette Stadium, hitting a new historic low against the Packers . Maye linked up with Tom Brady for an incredible photo but didn’t play quite up to the five-time Super Bowl champion’s standards in a losing effort. Maye was asked about his performance after the game in comments shared by Mike Reiss of ESPN NFL Nation. “Yeah, very…I’m disappointed in myself…We had (chances) to get back in the game, messed ’em up. We had a chance to get back to within three points multiple times, just frustrating. I’ve gotta do a better job from the whole perspective, I wasn’t good today, we gotta bounce back, and know that this was the game’s lesson, we’re battling.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Maye passed for 299 yards and three touchdowns, but his three interceptions stood out like a sore thumb on a day when New England coughed the football up four times compared to zero for Matt LaFleur’s Packers. Maye’s team converted 4-of-9 third downs but also gave up four sacks and fell behind the eight-ball by a score of 14-0 after one quarter. Coach Mike Vrabel ’s Patriots seem content to stand pat with the team they have heading toward Tuesday, November 10’s trade deadline, but there seems to be a lot missing with New England right now and AJ Brown’s injury absence is just one part of it. TreVeyon Henderson’s absence isn’t helping, either, but the Patriots have to play better football regardless of their starting lineup, and Maye knows it. Related: Patriots’ Christian Gonzalez shares tough admission after getting lit up by Packers Related: Patriots hit historic low vs. Packers as Tom Brady watches from booth

item.title: After joining OKC, Nique Clifford pens goodbye message to Kings: 'Truly blessed'
item.description: Continuing to shuffle their duct-taped roster, the Oklahoma City Thunder added another piece to fortify their depth. They acquired Nique Clifford from the Sacramento Kings for two future second-round picks. This signals another buy-low move on cheap, cost-controlled young talent. In his second season, Clifford had fallen out of favor with the Kings. He was outside of their rotation. That's after a surprisingly-productive rookie year. He's averaged 7.9 points on 41.6% shooting, 3.5 rebounds and 2.3 assists in his career. He was the No. 24 pick of the 2025 NBA draft. Only 83 games into his NBA career, Clifford has experienced the cold-hearted business side of things. His time on the Kings was short — specifically, for a first-round pick. But now, he gets a fresh opportunity on the Thunder. The 24-year-old said his goodbyes to Sacramento after the trade was made official. Clifford wrote on his Instagram story: "Thank you Sac for everything in my short time here! Truly blessed for all the experiences and memories. Wish I could've done more for yall" Clifford then flipped the page to the next chapter of his NBA journey with the Thunder. It'll be interesting to see where he falls in OKC's rotation. The defense-first forward should add to that side of the ball, but his career 32.6% 3-point shot suggests the offense is still a work in progress — and a negative, if you're cynical. Obviously, Clifford will need time to adjust to his new NBA home and role. He goes from the worst team in the league to a recent NBA champion and constant title contender. Season-altering injuries to Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren and Cason Wallace have shaken things up a bit. This deal is the latest example of that ripple effect. item.title: Patriots vs. Packers Takeaways: 5 Things That Went Wrong in Week 9 Loss
item.description: Patriots vs. Packers Takeaways: 5 Things That Went Wrong in Week 9 Loss originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots couldn't keep pace with the Green Bay Packers on Sunday, falling 45-27 at Gillette Stadium in Week 9. New England had opportunities to make things interesting offensively, with Drake Maye throwing three touchdown passes. However, four turnovers proved too costly against a Green Bay offense that took advantage of the mistakes and consistently found room to operate. The Patriots struggled to slow down Jordan Love and Green Bay's passing attack, allowing the Packers to put up 45 points and hand New England its fourth loss of the season. Here are five takeaways from the Patriots' loss to the Packers. Drake Maye's Turnovers Overshadow Productive Passing Day Maye put together a productive statistical performance, but his mistakes played a significant part in Sunday's loss. The Patriots quarterback completed 21 of 38 passes for 299 yards and three touchdowns. He connected with Rhamondre Stevenson for a 30-yard score in the second quarter before finding Efton Chism III and Mack Hollins for touchdowns later in the game. However, Maye also threw three interceptions, all coming in the first half. Green Bay capitalized on the turnovers, building a 24-14 halftime lead after taking advantage of New England's early mistakes. The three interceptions were a notable setback for Maye, who had put together a strong stretch of performances entering the matchup. Evan Williams Somehow Stays In Bounds On This Interception, Picking Off Drake Maye. Dude Literally Came Out Of Nowhere After It Was Tipped In The Air And Still Managed To Hang On. His Interception Is Amazing, Especially The Way He Kept His Feet In On The Sideline. https://t.co/xBAMHUUxDH — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) November 8, 2026 Although he continued making plays through the air, the Patriots couldn't afford to give Green Bay that many extra opportunities. Christian Gonzalez Has Difficult Afternoon Against Packers Receivers Christian Gonzalez had one of his toughest outings of the season against Green Bay. The Patriots cornerback was tasked with helping contain a Packers receiving group that presented plenty of challenges, but Jordan Love repeatedly found success against New England's secondary. According to Pro Football Focus , Gonzalez allowed 10 receptions on 11 targets for 187 yards and a touchdown. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson both found success against the Patriots cornerback, combining for 335 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Green Bay capitalized on the turnovers, building a 24-14 halftime lead after taking advantage of New England's early mistakes. The three interceptions were a notable setback for Maye, who had put together a strong stretch of performances entering the matchup. Christian Gonzalez Has Difficult Afternoon Against Packers Receivers Christian Gonzalez had one of his toughest outings of the season against Green Bay. The Patriots cornerback was tasked with helping contain a Packers receiving group that presented plenty of challenges, but Jordan Love repeatedly found success against New England's secondary. According to Pro Football Focus , Gonzalez allowed 10 receptions on 11 targets for 187 yards and a touchdown. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson both found success against the Patriots cornerback, combining for 335 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Christian Gonzalez was COOKED today by Christian Watson and Matthew Golden 🚨 👨‍🍳11 targets 👨‍🍳10 receptions 👨‍🍳187 yards 👨‍🍳1 touchdown Watson: 👨‍🍳3 targets 👨‍🍳3 receptions allowed 👨‍🍳82 yards allowed 👨‍🍳1 TD allowed Golden: 👨‍🍳7 targets 👨‍🍳7 receptions allowed 👨‍🍳105 yards allowed https://t.co/dsocUsvPmu — Football Forever (@fballforeverhq) November 9, 2026 Golden was particularly effective early, recording six catches for 126 yards and a touchdown in the first quarter alone. It was an uncharacteristic showing for one of New England's top defensive players. Gonzalez will need to bounce back as the Patriots prepare for another difficult matchup against Detroit. Patriots Defense Gets Exposed by Packers' Explosive Offense New England's defensive struggles extended well beyond Gonzalez. The Patriots had no consistent answer for Love, who completed 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards and three touchdowns. He also added a rushing touchdown as Green Bay repeatedly found ways to move the ball downfield. OH. MY. GOSH. 📺: FOX https://t.co/sIjdR4nvd1 — Green Bay Packers (@packers) November 8, 2026 Watson and Golden did most of the damage through the air. Watson finished with seven receptions for 171 yards and a touchdown, while Golden recorded 10 catches for 164 yards and a score. The Patriots also struggled to contain Green Bay on the ground, surrendering 129 rushing yards. The Packers entered Sunday with one of the league's least productive rushing attacks but found success in multiple areas against New England. Green Bay finished with 478 total yards, converted four of five red-zone opportunities and became the first opponent to score 45 points at Gillette Stadium. It was a particularly concerning performance for a Patriots defense that will have to regroup quickly before facing another explosive offense in Detroit. Patriots Turnovers Give Packers Too Many Opportunities New England's mistakes went beyond Maye's interceptions. The Patriots committed four turnovers, with Stevenson losing a fumble in addition to Maye's three interceptions. Green Bay took advantage of the extra opportunities, scoring after New England's mistakes and making it difficult for the Patriots to build any momentum. Make that four turnovers forced by the @Packers' defense today 🧀 GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus https://t.co/518z9K6SWP — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Stevenson's fumble was particularly costly, setting up a touchdown reception for Watson. The running back also left the game with a knee injury after catching a touchdown pass later in the matchup. The Patriots had a difficult time recovering from their early mistakes, falling behind 24-7 before cutting the deficit to 24-14 at halftime. Against an offense as explosive as Green Bay's, New England couldn't afford to keep giving the Packers favorable field position. The turnovers ultimately made an already difficult matchup even tougher for the Patriots to overcome. Patriots' Receiving Group Shows Signs of Life Despite Loss There were some positives for New England's offense, particularly from its receiving group. Maye connected with three different Patriots for touchdown receptions, including Stevenson, Chism and Hollins. DeMario Douglas also delivered a strong performance, finishing with five catches for 102 yards to lead New England's receiving group. Hollins made an impact in his return to the lineup, hauling in a 22-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter. Chism also contributed five catches for 49 yards and a score. However, the Patriots managed just 94 rushing yards as a team, making it difficult to find balance offensively. New England will need more from its ground game moving forward, especially if it wants to take some of the pressure off Maye. The Patriots will look to regroup next week when they travel to Germany to face the Detroit Lions. item.title: Huawei says it’s made a 100 percent Chinese PC
item.description: Huawei claims it’s built a desktop PC that uses only parts made in CHina. The company launched the Qingyun HM650 last week and said it uses Huawei’s own Kirin X90 processor, a ten-core 20-thread machine with a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The machine runs a newly developed enterprise version of HarmonyOS, the OS Huawei developed to end its dependence on Android and which it intends to run on most of the devices it makes. A single Chinese government agency has reportedly signed up for 600 of the machines. That’s not an indication this machine is a curiosity, because Beijing has ordered all government entities to shift from Wintel boxes to local alternatives. While Huawei has reportedly claimed local companies manufactured 100 percent of the components in the machine, it is unclear if all those components use Chinese designs. The Register mentions that uncertainty as many non-Chinese companies continue to operate factories in China. Even if Huawei is using some parts that aren’t entirely Chinese, the debut of the Qingyun HM650 is bad news for Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm, as all are suffering as the PC market shrinks due to the rising cost of memory. China’s government is an enormous buyer, and losing the chance to bid for its business is unlikely to be helpful. Japan announces emergency response package after wave of cyberattacks Japan’s government last Friday announced emergency funding to help local organizations strengthen the nation's cyber-defences. The ¥10 billion ($63 million) package follows a wave of cyberattacks that have disrupted railways, retailers, KFC’s logistics provider , and cloud computing operators . The emergency package aims to help Japanese government agencies to use AI to nail infosec basics, and to build tools that let the National Cybersecurity Office aggregate information about cyberattacks. Some funds will also go towards supporting victims. Lenovo’s APAC boss shifts to lead Motorola Lenovo is looking for a new leader of its Asia-Pacific operations after shifting the boss, Amar Babu, to a role as mobile business group general manager and global president at Motorola. Amar led Lenovo in the region for over five years and the company credited him with turning it into “a more balanced and diversified business and a key growth engine.” “Across the portfolio, AP maintained its #1 PC position, while our mobile business achieved notable growth, with Motorola reaching nearly 9 percent market share in India and the #2 smartphone OEM in Japan,” according to a company announcement . “Our infrastructure business achieved profitable growth and nearly double-digit market share, while Solutions & Services continued to strengthen its best-of-breed industry position and significantly increased its advanced services business mix to over 50 percent.” Lenovo has not named a new leader for its APAC outpost. Some funds will also go towards supporting victims. Lenovo’s APAC boss shifts to lead Motorola Lenovo is looking for a new leader of its Asia-Pacific operations after shifting the boss, Amar Babu, to a role as mobile business group general manager and global president at Motorola. Vietnam hails homegrown USB storage chip Vietnam’s government last week announced the nation’s first domestically-designed security chip - a 28-nanometer device that apparently integrates encryption algorithms in silicon. The chip is already in use on secure USB storage devices that Vietnam’s government employs to store info for government and defense agencies, plus the Communist Party. The nation hopes to use the chips to secure storage of the national digital signature certification system, and critical infrastructure systems in electricity, water, oil and gas, and telecommunications. Hanoi says the chip needs more testing before the government will trust it to protect state secrets, but hailed the chip as an important step towards development of sovereign security capabilities. Apple’s biggest ever education deal Apple last week quietly announced it has won its biggest-ever sale of Macs into the education market in the Philippines. Speaking on the company’s Q4 earnings call, CEO John Ternus said Apple sold 172,000 MacBook Neos to the Department of Education in the Philippines, which will deploy them to teachers and staff. ®

item.title: 📹 After exit, coach sees a way for Vasco to be great again
item.description: 📹 After exit, coach sees a way for Vasco to be great again This Sunday (8), Vasco fans suffered yet another disappointment this season. After their traumatic elimination from the CONMEBOL Sudamericana against Boca Juniors at a packed Maracanã, the Cruz-Maltino also crashed out of the Copa do Brasil semifinals, this time against Palmeiras on penalties at São Januário. Speaking in the press room afterward, coach Pedro Emanuel expressed pride in Vasco's run in the tournament. The 51-year-old Portuguese coach, who joined the Gigante da Colina in July this year and is under contract until December 2027, stressed that frustrating exits like those Vasco suffered this season are part of the rebuilding process for "teams that were once great and want to be great again" . "Football is as magical as it is cruel. And today was a cruel day for us. It could have been magical. We were seconds away from it being magical for us. It was magical for Palmeiras and cruel for us. What I take away from this Copa (do Brasil) is pride in our journey and the way we went out. Together with our fans, we built up great expectations for this competition. It's an important competition, and we knew that and wanted to deliver that for them. And I think, in the end, when we all left the pitch, we felt sad because we really did everything within our power to reach the final. And today was a true final. There was a very capable, very talented team on the other side. And this is also part of the growth of teams like Vasco, who were once great and want to be great again. This is the path we have to follow." Pedro Emanuel also made a point of recalling an interview with Arsenal's Brazilian defender Gabriel Magalhães, who noted that the Gunners had to settle for second place for four consecutive seasons before becoming Premier League champions again. "Today (Sunday), I saw the comments from Arsenal defender Gabriel (Magalhães). He said they finished runners-up four times in England and managed to find the formula to win on the fifth attempt." This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇧🇷 here.

item.title: Studs and duds from Houston’s 44-22 win against the Chargers
item.description: The Houston Texans put up their best performance of the season in their 44-22 win against the Los Angeles Chargers. Houston’s offense look unstoppable, going three for four in the red zone and scoring five touchdowns. Los Angeles also turned the ball over twice, which helped the Texans get this victory. You could tell from the first drive of the game that Houston was going to have a good day offensively. The 7th-ranked passing attack marched down the field in eight plays, going 73 yards for their first touchdown of the night. Quarterback CJ Stroud had one blemish in the second quarter when he threw an interception, but was otherwise near-perfect, throwing for a season-high 386 yards and tying his career-best with five touchdown passes. Defensively, they disrupted the Chargers’ offense all game with eight sacks and two takeaways. Through the first three quarters, Los Angeles only had nine points. They ended up benching their quarterback, Justin Herbert, before the end of the game. Here are the studs and duds from Houston’s third win of the season, including Stroud who threw a career-high five touchdown passes in this win and wide receiver Kayshon Boutte who had a career-high 125 receiving yards. Stud: QB C.J. Stroud Coming into this game, the Los Angeles Chargers were supposed to be a top-10 passing defense, but CJ Stroud completely shredded them. Los Angeles only allowed eight passing touchdowns in the first seven games, but Stroud had five passing touchdowns, tying his career-high. There was no stopping Stroud and the passing offense in this game. This just added to Stroud’s great performance this season. Dud: RB Woody Marks It is not like Houston needed to run the ball, but the offense was hoping to exploit Los Angeles’ statistically poor run defense. Instead, the run was barely able to get over 100 yards. Woody Marks only had 70 rushing yards, averaging 3.9 yards per attempt, including two runs over 10 yards. This is not terrible, but they need more out of the run game going forward and Marks is probably going to be the answer since David Montgomery was not doing much before his injury. Stud: WR Kayshon Boutte Boutte was essentially a non-factor for Houston’s offense before the bye week. But in this game, he emerged as the Texans’ leading receiver with four receptions for 125 yards and two touchdowns. It was just his third career game with at least 100 yards. His 63-yard touchdown was tied with Tank Dell’s touchdown earlier in the game for Houston’s longest touchdown of the season. Dud: WR Marvin Harrison Jr The Texans had an offensive explosion against the Chargers, especially in the passing game. However, Harrison was barely involved. He was only targeted three times and had two receptions for 20 yards. This was really disappointing after scoring a touchdown in Houston’s last game. Still, not everyone can get targets, so maybe this just was not his week. Perhaps Harrison will get more touches next week against the Cleveland Browns. Stud: WR

This is not terrible, but they need more out of the run game going forward and Marks is probably going to be the answer since David Montgomery was not doing much before his injury. Stud: WR Kayshon Boutte Boutte was essentially a non-factor for Houston’s offense before the bye week. But in this game, he emerged as the Texans’ leading receiver with four receptions for 125 yards and two touchdowns. It was just his third career game with at least 100 yards. His 63-yard touchdown was tied with Tank Dell’s touchdown earlier in the game for Houston’s longest touchdown of the season. Dud: WR Marvin Harrison Jr The Texans had an offensive explosion against the Chargers, especially in the passing game. However, Harrison was barely involved. He was only targeted three times and had two receptions for 20 yards. This was really disappointing after scoring a touchdown in Houston’s last game. Still, not everyone can get targets, so maybe this just was not his week. Perhaps Harrison will get more touches next week against the Cleveland Browns. Stud: WR Tank Dell It was amazing to see Dell get his first catch in Houston’s last game against the New York Giants. But seeing his electric speed on his 63-yard touchdown was something else entirely. Despite barely being back from his gruesome 2024 knee injury, Dell stepped up and finished with four receptions for 105 yards, along with the touchdown reception. It was also his second-longest touchdown of his NFL career. Dud: DE Danielle Hunter Not only did CJ Stroud shred the Chargers’ defense, but the Texans’ defense demolished Los Angeles’ offensive line with a total of eight sacks in the game. MJ Stewart and Logan Hall each had a sack while Sheldon Rankins, Jadeveon Clowney and Will Anderson Jr all had two sacks each. However, Hunter did not have a sack. In fact, he only had one solo tackle. After having 15 sacks last year, Hunter’s production has really declined this season, at least to his standard since joining the Texans in 2024. Stud: CB Derek Stingley Jr It has been hard for Houston’s defense to get takeaways this season, but cornerback Derek got an interception in this game, which helped set up Nico Collins’ touchdown. Justin Herbert has been having a terrible season, so it is not surprising that someone got an interception for the Texans. But for Stingley to get his first of the season was good to see, especially since he had four last season and was being counted on to play a large role in this Houston defense. Stud: WR Nico Collins Speaking of Collins’ touchdown, that was one of the best catches you will see all season. How Collins managed to catch the ball with one hand and still get down in bounds is amazing. Only a stud could make that kind of play. This article originally appeared on Texans Wire: Studs and duds from Houston’s 44-22 win against the Chargers

item.title: LeBron James’ Statement On His Family’s Safety After Arrested Stalker Claims To Be His Son
item.description: Nov 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) reacts and celebrates a three point shot against the Chicago Bulls during the second half at United Center. Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images A man was recently arrested for allegedly stalking LeBron James’ LA home and claiming to be his son after trespassing on the property. The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Chicago Bulls 127-121 tonight after a nail-biting matchup that was decided in the closing stretch of the game. James finished with 22 points, five rebounds, and five assists while shooting 8-16 from the field (50.0% FG) and 2-5 from behind the three-point line (40.0% 3P). Following the win, LeBron James spoke to the media scrum in the locker room and addressed the reported arrest. “My family is safe, and that’s the most important. We’re still looking into everything,” James said in the 76ers’ locker room. According to TMZ, the suspect was caught while seemingly trespassing on LeBron James’ property when the star or his family were not at home. “Law enforcement sources tell TMZ, security called the cops around 9 PM Friday after catching a male suspect on the property on one of their security cameras. After the LAPD showed up, they arrested the alleged suspect for stalking,” TMZ reported. “Oddly enough, the suspect claimed to believe he is LeBron’s son during his chat with cops. Thankfully, LeBron wasn’t home at the time as LBJ was playing with the 76ers against the Cleveland Cavaliers in Ohio. We’re told the suspect didn’t make entry into the residence and that a police report for stalking was taken,” they concluded . This comes after a string of robberies has been observed that have targeted athletes over the past few years. But while the alleged stalker did not manage to get inside the building, his presence created a fear of potential robbery as well. So it is natural for LeBron James to worry mainly about his family’s safety before considering baseless or outrageous claims like having a fourth child. LeBron James has three children with his wife, Savannah James, namely Bronny, Bryce, and Zhuri James. And while there is no proof that anything the stalker claims is true, we live in a generation where information not directly refuted becomes fact for most people. Therefore, James should be encouraged to directly refute any of the stalker’s claims. In the end, James stated unequivocally that his family’s safety is still his top priority as things develop. The intrusion into the NBA superstar’s private property is the more worrisome issue, even though his outrageous claims have garnered attention. Hopefully, going forward, Los Angeles authorities can guarantee James and his family’s safety.

item.title: San Francisco 49ers Make Christian McCaffrey Announcement Amid Raiders Game
item.description: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 08: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers runs the ball against the Las Vegas Raiders during the first quarter at Levi's Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Getty The San Francisco 49ers are back from their bye week and facing the Las Vegas Raiders at Levi’s Stadium on Sunday afternoon. Even with several key players, including Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Christian Kirk, sidelined, the 49ers offense didn’t miss a beat in the first half. Much of that success came from the dominance of running back Christian McCaffrey. McCaffrey serves as a workhorse in the backfield as a runner, but he’s also a safety blanket for quarterback Brock Purdy as a pass catcher. 49ers Make Announcement on McCaffrey San Francisco took a 21-10 lead into halftime, and McCaffrey made some NFL history during the first two quarters. He rushed 13 times for 56 yards and a touchdown while adding one reception for 12 yards and another touchdown through the air. That performance put him in an exclusive category of his own. After McCaffrey scored his second touchdown, the 49ers announced that he now holds the record for the most receiving touchdowns by a running back in the Super Bowl era. “He’s sitting at the top,” the 49ers posted on X. He’s sitting at the top 🙌 https://t.co/fp67iy54gZ — San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) November 8, 2026 4 9ers Fans React on Social Media The 49ers fanbase reacted to the historic milestone achieved by their star running back. “Congrats CMC,” a fan said. Someone else added, “CMC Legendary.” Another person wrote, “Keep It Up!!!!” “WORD UP 23,” one more fan commented. McCaffrey’s NFL Career Drafted out of Stanford in 2017, McCaffrey has been one of the greatest tailbacks of his generation, and he hasn’t slowed down one bit at age 30. This season, he entered Sunday with 84 carries for 389 yards and eight touchdowns, while hauling in 34 receptions for 251 yards. On Sunday, his rushing touchdown marked the 71st of his career, while the historic receiving touchdown gave him 37 for his career. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post San Francisco 49ers Make Christian McCaffrey Announcement Amid Raiders Game appeared first on HEAVY .

This season, he entered Sunday with 84 carries for 389 yards and eight touchdowns, while hauling in 34 receptions for 251 yards. On Sunday, his rushing touchdown marked the 71st of his career, while the historic receiving touchdown gave him 37 for his career. item.title: Another QB injury: Drew Lock’s status ‘up in the air’ for Week 10 vs. Raiders
item.description: It might be Jalen Milroe time for the Seattle Seahawks. While Drew Lock didn’t miss any game action during Seattle’s 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals, he has a new injury on top of the severe tendinitis he reportedly had been battling over the past couple of weeks. Lock was seen grabbing his right hip area during the third quarter of Sunday’s game, grimacing and walking gingerly as he got off the field prior to Seattle’s final scoring drive. Jalen Milroe warmed up on the sidelines while Lock went into the blue tent, but Lock stayed in for the rest of the afternoon and didn’t miss a play. Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald told reporters at the post-game press conference that Lock’s status is “up in the air” after getting his oblique looked at. “We’re looking at him for an oblique, so we’ll assess it and go from there,” Macdonald said. “He made it out [of the game], but you know, like I’ve sat here before and told you a guy would be ready and then he wasn’t. So, leave my options open.” For what it’s worth, Lock said “we’ll get it looked at [Sunday night]” and that it “was not too bad.” When asked if the injury affected him, he said, “I wouldn’t say it did.” The Seahawks talk about having a “70-man roster,” knowing they’ll frequently need contributions from beyond the 53. With six starters down, this was one of those weeks. Mike Macdonald said it showed “the power of our 70” and called Drew Lock “a beast” for playing through injury. pic.twitter.com/rp7ZM3vgeo — Brady Henderson (@BradyHenderson) November 9, 2026 Lock also said he felt “good” playing through the elbow injury. Odds are not sounding favorable for Sam Darnold to return against the Las Vegas Raiders, with ESPN’s Adam Schefter reporting what felt like a pretty obvious situation that he is in “jeopardy” of missing Week 10 with quad and rib injuries. If Darnold was listed as “week-to-week” by Mike Macdonald, this isn’t earth-shattering news as much as it affirms what’s already been said. If the news is negative on Lock, then we could see Jalen Milroe’s first career NFL start. But at the minimum, this is a very banged up Seahawks quarterback room and the bye week might be one of the most welcome byes in recent Seahawks history.

item.title: 2027: APC chieftain laments 73% voter apathy in Aramoko
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and member of the President Bola Tinubu/APC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council, Engineer Atinuke Owolabi, has expressed concern over the low voter turnout in Aramoko-Ekiti during the 2023 presidential election, saying about 73 per cent of registered voters in the community did not participate. Owolabi, who is also the convener of PBAT-MOB Aramoko Community Engagement, spoke during an APC voter education exercise and community engagement in Aramoko, Ekiti Central Senatorial District, over the weekend. The programme, organised in support of the re-election bids of President Tinubu and Senate Leader, Senator Michael Opeyemi Bamidele, was held under the theme, “My Vote, My Voice”. She also represents the South-West as a member of the North Central Development Commission. Owolabi said voter education was essential to strengthening democracy, particularly in rural communities where inadequate information about electoral procedures could discourage participation or lead to invalid votes. Presenting figures from the 2023 presidential election, she said Ekiti State had 988,923 registered voters, out of whom 315,058 were accredited, while 308,171 valid votes were recorded and 6,301 ballots were rejected. She said available ward-level records for Aramoko I and Aramoko II showed a combined 17,426 registered voters, compared with 4,680 votes reportedly cast during the presidential election. According to her, the figures indicated that approximately 12,746 registered voters did not participate, representing about 73 per cent of the electorate in the two wards. She urged residents to improve their participation in future elections, stressing the need for the community to translate its voting strength into meaningful democratic engagement. Owolabi said the exercise was designed to educate residents on voting procedures, encourage participation and reduce the number of rejected ballots. The programme also featured the unveiling of a voter education handbook intended to guide residents on electoral processes, identification of polling units and the proper use of their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs). She said: “I believe voter education is key. If we cannot completely eliminate rejected votes, we should at least be able to reduce them in Ekiti State, particularly in Aramoko, my community. “We are here to sensitise our people on the correct way to vote. When they go to the polling units, they must ensure that they vote correctly. “We have the population, and we have the voters. What is really lacking is adequate information. Our people need to understand the right way to vote. “Today, we have unveiled a voter education handbook, which is a welcome development. Through this handbook, our people will be taught what elections are all about. item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang starring in possible remake of The Spy Who Shagged Me
item.description: Nvidia’s board has opened an investigation into its CEO Jensen Huang after he admitted to an affair, amid allegations he had a commercial relationship with a woman US authorities feel is likely a Chinese spy. The AI hardware giant’s board published a statement on Sunday afternoon that states it is “initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” The New York Times is the source of that reporting . On October 29 it alleged US government intelligence agencies decided to investigate a woman who goes by Alice Huang and/or Huang Le, on grounds she passes intelligence with Beijing. In that story The Times used the term “close relationship” to describe the Nvidia CEO's associations with both Ms Huang and US president Donald Trump. On Sunday the newspaper alleged US authorities believe Alice Huang and Jensen Huang shared a "romantic" relationship. The Times further alleges Ms Huang is a Chinese citizen who worked for a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed that has bought plenty of Nvidia hardware and is suspected of doing so to make it available to Chinese users, either by running inside datacenters or facilitating transport to the Middle Kingdom. The US has for years banned or restricted exports of advanced GPUs to China, partly because it feels Beijing’s armed forces can use them to build systems that will erode America’s military superiority. Any relationship, of any sort, between Jensen Huang and a Chinese intelligence operative would therefore be enormously concerning. The company told The Times that Jensen Huang and Alice Huang just had normal CEO-to-customer-exec chats that were no threat to Nvidia intellectual property or US national security. Shortly after Nvidia’s board published its statement, Huang sent an email to staff that the company made public . “I owe my family and all of you an apology,” the email opens. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Huang’s email doesn’t explicitly link his actions to The Times’ reports, but he says he supports the Nvidia board’s decision to open its investigation “and will cooperate fully.” “I love our country and our company,” Huang wrote. “I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.” The CEO’s mail, and the Board’s statement, make no allegations about any “close relationship” with Ms. Huang. The exact nature of that relationship therefore remains mysterious, as does Nvidia’s relationship with Singapore, a tiny island nation that has sometimes been the source of 22 percent of the company’s revenue. item.dc:creator: Simon Sharwood
item.content:encoded: Nvidia’s board has opened an investigation into its CEO Jensen Huang after he admitted to an affair, amid allegations he had a commercial relationship with a woman US authorities feel is likely a Chinese spy. The AI hardware giant’s board published a statement on Sunday afternoon that states it is “initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” The New York Times is the source of that reporting . On October 29 it alleged US government intelligence agencies decided to investigate a woman who goes by Alice Huang and/or Huang Le, on grounds she passes intelligence with Beijing. In that story The Times used the term “close relationship” to describe the Nvidia CEO's associations with both Ms Huang and US president Donald Trump. On Sunday the newspaper alleged US authorities believe Alice Huang and Jensen Huang shared a "romantic" relationship. The Times further alleges Ms Huang is a Chinese citizen who worked for a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed that has bought plenty of Nvidia hardware and is suspected of doing so to make it available to Chinese users, either by running inside datacenters or facilitating transport to the Middle Kingdom. The US has for years banned or restricted exports of advanced GPUs to China, partly because it feels Beijing’s armed forces can use them to build systems that will erode America’s military superiority. Any relationship, of any sort, between Jensen Huang and a Chinese intelligence operative would therefore be enormously concerning. The company told The Times that Jensen Huang and Alice Huang just had normal CEO-to-customer-exec chats that were no threat to Nvidia intellectual property or US national security. Shortly after Nvidia’s board published its statement, Huang sent an email to staff that the company made public . “I owe my family and all of you an apology,” the email opens. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Huang’s email doesn’t explicitly link his actions to The Times’ reports, but he says he supports the Nvidia board’s decision to open its investigation “and will cooperate fully.” “I love our country and our company,” Huang wrote. “I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.” The CEO’s mail, and the Board’s statement, make no allegations about any “close relationship” with Ms. Huang. The exact nature of that relationship therefore remains mysterious, as does Nvidia’s relationship with Singapore, a tiny island nation that has sometimes been the source of 22 percent of the company’s revenue. Singapore is simply incapable of hosting as much Nvidia kit as that volume of purchases would buy, because its government limits datacenters to 1.6 GW of energy consumption. When asked to explain that oddity, Nvidia has said that it’s satisfied Singaporean entities buy its hardware on behalf of end-users in other locations, and that such deals are not used to evade the USA’s sanctions. Nvidia is not a notably scandal-prone company, but in 2022 it did admit to having previously misrepresented the impact of cryptocurrency mining on sales of its gaming hardware. China has opened an antitrust case , and US authorities may have considered doing likewise . Jensen Huang, however, has never presented as the kind of CEO who makes operating at the edge of the law a regular tactic. Nor does he hold sufficient Nvidia shares or voting power to unilaterally make major decisions. This leaves the leader of the world’s top AI company appearing to have made a very human error. ®

item.title: Aba South establishes commercial farms to boost revenue, create jobs
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Aba South Local Government Area of Abia State has established commercial poultry and piggery farms as part of efforts to boost its internally generated revenue (IGR), create jobs and equip residents with skills in animal husbandry. The Executive Chairman of the council, Chief Obialo Anyanwu, disclosed this while briefing journalists on his administration’s two-year achievements, explaining that the initiative was aimed at making the local government more financially self-reliant. Anyanwu said his administration was exploring sustainable revenue sources to strengthen the council’s capacity to deliver services rather than depend entirely on external funding. He explained that the farms would also serve as training centres where residents would acquire practical skills in animal farming, enabling them to establish their own businesses and employ others. He said: “We don’t believe in all these 10kg of rice empowerment. What we want in Aba South is giving our people that level of empowerment that will make them self-sustaining and employ others. So, we’ll teach the techniques needed to succeed in the business. “The three buildings in the poultry section are up, two are already roofed, and the staff quarters are at the lintel stage because it’s a proper farm and people must reside there. “Possibly by the end of the year, everything will take off. So, we’re envisaging such a future. We, as the third tier of government, must stand for ourselves, and it has pushed us into doing commercial poultry and commercial pig farming.” The chairman disclosed that the poultry farm occupies 14 plots of land, while the piggery farm covers seven plots. He added that the projects would generate revenue for the council, create employment opportunities and provide practical agricultural training for residents, including staff of the council’s agriculture department. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Aba South Local Government Area of Abia State has established commercial poultry and piggery farms as part of efforts to boost its internally generated revenue (IGR), create jobs and equip residents with skills in animal husbandry. The Executive Chairman of the council, Chief Obialo Anyanwu, disclosed this while briefing journalists on his administration’s two-year achievements, explaining that the initiative was aimed at making the local government more financially self-reliant. Anyanwu said his administration was exploring sustainable revenue sources to strengthen the council’s capacity to deliver services rather than depend entirely on external funding. He explained that the farms would also serve as training centres where residents would acquire practical skills in animal farming, enabling them to establish their own businesses and employ others. He said: “We don’t believe in all these 10kg of rice empowerment. What we want in Aba South is giving our people that level of empowerment that will make them self-sustaining and employ others. So, we’ll teach the techniques needed to succeed in the business. “The three buildings in the poultry section are up, two are already roofed, and the staff quarters are at the lintel stage because it’s a proper farm and people must reside there. “Possibly by the end of the year, everything will take off. So, we’re envisaging such a future. We, as the third tier of government, must stand for ourselves, and it has pushed us into doing commercial poultry and commercial pig farming.” The chairman disclosed that the poultry farm occupies 14 plots of land, while the piggery farm covers seven plots. He added that the projects would generate revenue for the council, create employment opportunities and provide practical agricultural training for residents, including staff of the council’s agriculture department. On healthcare, Anyanwu said the council had established and equipped 22 Glycoster World Primary Healthcare Centres in partnership with the Abia State Government. He said the facilities had been commissioned and made operational, adding that the council had also organised free medical tests and treatments for residents. On education, the chairman said the council was supporting Governor Alex Otti’s free back-to-school programme through the distribution of 4,000 school bags to pupils in primary schools across the local government area. He explained that the initial target was 10,000 beneficiaries but that the distribution would be carried out in phases after an enumeration exercise showed that the number of eligible pupils exceeded the target. Anyanwu also disclosed that the council was partnering with the state government on primary school development, including the ongoing construction of a smart school along Etche Road. He said the administration had equally invested in digital skills training, with more than 130 residents trained in three cohorts. According to him, the first cohort graduated 50 participants, the second had 30, while the third produced another 50 graduates. On road infrastructure, Anyanwu said the council commenced road grading shortly after he assumed office on November 4, 2024. He disclosed that more than 20 kilometres of roads across the 12 wards were graded between late November 2024 and early January 2025, while another 28 kilometres were covered by the end of 2025. The chairman commended security agencies in the area for their professionalism and commitment, saying Aba South had remained peaceful. He identified the removal of individuals and companies allegedly operating unauthorised revenue collection arrangements as one of his administration’s major achievements. “One of the biggest achievements we’ve made in this administration so far was the chasing out of one revenue vampire with one company called Chicotax out of the Aba South LGA. He has been doing this for several years, but this time around, we’ve arrested the situation, and we’ve moved on,” he said. Anyanwu described the relationship between the council and the state government as cordial, commending Otti for supporting road infrastructure projects in Aba South. He expressed optimism that ongoing and planned road projects would improve transportation and access to several communities in the council area. He specifically mentioned the ongoing work on Obohia Road, which he said included a drainage system designed to channel floodwater from different parts of Aba into the river. He also listed Umuebeke Road, Uratta Road and Old Express Road among the projects expected to improve road connectivity in the area. The chairman said the projects, when completed, would improve access to communities and enable the Abia State Environmental Protection Agency (ASEPA) to extend its operations to previously inaccessible areas. item.title: Trump admits his mass deportation policy was ‘too tough’
item.description: US President Donald Trump said that his mass deportation of undocumented immigrants was “too tough,” according to an excerpt of an interview with CBS aired Sunday. Asked about his deportation policy, Trump told CBS’ “60 Minutes”: “I think it was too tough…I think it might be too tough.” The excerpt was published by CBS on X ahead of a broadcast of the interview on network TV later Sunday. It was recorded after the Republican Party’s heavy loss in midterm elections on Tuesday. While Trump has won some domestic support for securing the US southern border, his administration’s aggressive push to deport millions of undocumented migrants has drawn widespread criticism. However, Trump on Friday appointed the architect of that hardline policy, Stephen Miller, as his chief of staff on Friday, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback after the Republican election loss. Miller has been synonymous with scenes of masked immigration agents committing violence after he backed federal agents who shot and killed two Americans early this year. The post Trump admits his mass deportation policy was ‘too tough’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Barcelona move clear at the top after Fermín López’s double stuns Atlético Madrid
item.description: They had been in a battle, they had been behind and they had been on edge, but Barcelona found a way through, holding on to their place at the top of the table and holding the doubts at bay for another day. A fortnight in which they were defeated by Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid , in which they might have wondered if something was not right, ended with a 2-1 win at Atlético Madrid. This was a proper test and a proper game, 10 World Cup winners on the field and first place awaiting the winner, and at the end of an intense enjoyable night, that was Hansi Flick’s side. At a noisy Metropolitano, the atmosphere matching the occasion, against a frenetic Atlético side that went for the throat, Barcelona trailed to a Giuliano Simeone goal and for a while in a frenzied first half it looked like there may be no way back. But they found it, two goals from Fermín López either side of the break leading them to the kind of victory that brings a reward beyond the points. It hadn’t been easy but they had made it; ultimately, they might conclude they had found a way to manage it too, some satisfaction in the suffering, in how they resisted and re-established control amid the chaos. Continue reading...

item.title: Fan rushed to hospital after stadium stand collapses during Bodo/Glimt match
item.description: A fan of Norwegian football club Bodo/Glimt has been hospitalised after the away end partially collapsed during their team’s fixture at Tromso, police said on Sunday. “Four people were confirmed to be involved, and one of them has been taken to the hospital,” the statement said. item.title: Sultan directs Muslims to sight Jumada Assaniya moon Monday
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO – The Sultanate Council of Sokoto has called on Muslims across Nigeria to search for the new crescent moon of Jumada Assaniya 1448AH on Monday, November 9, 2026. The directive was contained in a statement dated November 8, 2026, signed by Professor Sambo Wali Junaidu and made available to journalists on Sunday. According to the statement, the Advisory Committee on Religious Affairs of the Sultanate Council identified Monday as the 29th day of Jumada al-Ula 1448AH and the appropriate date for the nationwide moon-sighting exercise. The council urged Muslims across the country to actively participate in the exercise by looking out for the new crescent moon after sunset on Monday. It specifically requested anyone who sights the crescent to promptly report the observation to the nearest District or Village Head for onward transmission to His Eminence, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, CFR, mni, the Sultan of Sokoto and President-General of the Nigeria Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA). The council stressed the importance of timely and credible reports of confirmed sightings to enable the Sultan to make the appropriate religious announcement on the commencement of the new Islamic month. It noted that the Sultan remains the recognised authority responsible for communicating the outcome of the moon-sighting exercise to Muslims across the country. The announcement underscores the role of the Sultanate Council in coordinating Islamic religious affairs and guiding the Muslim Ummah on matters concerning the Islamic lunar calendar. In a prayer, Professor Sambo Wali Junaidu, Waziri and Chairman of the Advisory Committee on Religious Affairs of the Sultanate Council, asked Allah (SWT) to grant Muslims the guidance and strength to discharge the religious responsibility successfully. The council also prayed for divine assistance and acceptance of the exercise, urging Muslims to approach the assignment with sincerity, vigilance and a strong sense of religious commitment. The post Sultan directs Muslims to sight Jumada Assaniya moon Monday appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Fermin brace earns Liga leaders Barcelona 2-1 win at Atletico
item.description: Fermin Lopez struck twice to help Barcelona come from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 and move three points clear at the top of La Liga. The Spanish champions lead second place Real Madrid, who beat Valencia 3-0 on Saturday, with Atletico third, now five points behind. Giuliano Simeone fired Atletico ahead in a high-octane start, before Lopez pulled Barca level shortly before the interval at the Metropolitano stadium. The 23-year-old Spain international netted the winner after 66 minutes when Lamine Yamal slipped him in. The match started at a fast pace and both teams hit the woodwork in the opening stages. Alvarez, who tried and failed to force a move from Atletico to Barca in the summer, rounded goalkeeper Joan Garcia but could not finish off the chance as the defence blocked his route to goal. From the resulting corner Atletico defender Marc Pubill headed against the crossbar with Garcia beaten. At the other end Pedri crashed a strike against the woodwork after being fed by Barca’s teenage star Lamine Yamal. Atletico took the lead in the 10th minute, slicing Barca’s defence open. Alvarez crossed for Giuliano Simeone to turn home from close range. The game settled down after that pulsating start, although Alvarez came close to scoring Atletico’s second. The Argentine international’s shot was fumbled by Garcia, but the goalkeeper was able to collect the ball quickly afterwards. Yamal blasted into the side-netting from a tight angle with Barcelona not able to click into their top gears. Despite their struggles they went in level at the break, with a goal out of nowhere. Lopez’s path to the box was blocked but the ball bounced loose to the midfielder and he quickly smashed a strike past Jan Oblak. Early in the second half Alvarez lobbed over the crossbar when running in on goal. The forward came to rue the miss when Barcelona took the lead. Yamal played a clever pass through Atletico’s defence and Lopez kept his cool to beat Oblak. It was his seventh league goal in 11 top flight appearances this season. Barcelona kept Atletico at bay well in the final stages to take three points home from the capital before the international break. Earlier on fourth-place Real Betis earned a 2-0 win at Elche, while Real Sociedad, fifth, defeated Rayo Vallecano 1-0. Villarreal beat Getafe 2-0 to move eighth and Celta Vigo and Levante shared a goalless draw. The post Fermin brace earns Liga leaders Barcelona 2-1 win at Atletico appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027 Elections: Lagos APC Candidate Hamzat Promises 4,000 CNG Buses, 77 Electric Ferries
item.description: The Lagos State governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Obafemi Hamzat, has promised to deploy 4,000 compressed natural gas (CNG) buses to move one million passengers daily as part of plans to ease transportation challenges in the state. Hamzat, the incumbent Deputy Governor, also disclosed plans to expand water transportation with 77 electric ferries and improve connectivity between different parts of Lagos through an integrated transport system. ﻿ He made the promises on Sunday during the Lagos governorship debate organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, comprising Channels Television, TVC News, Punch Newspaper, The Cable, and Vanguard Newspaper. Explaining his transportation plans, Hamzat said the objective was to reduce commuting time and give residents more opportunities to rest and spend time with their families. “The plan is to give back time to the citizens to plan, to rest, to spend with their family. There’s nowhere in Africa that the private sector has funded a rail. “Since BRT started, it has done 77 million journeys; that is with 1,000 buses. My plan says we will push it to 4,000 buses; the idea is to move one million people a day with 4,000 CNG buses, meaning up to 5,000, create BRt lane from Marina to Epe, from Marina to Badagry and so on and so forth,” he said. “Today, over four million people have the Cowry card. What does that mean? It means you can use ferry, you can use rail, and you can use BRT buses — one payment — so that we can deal with how to subsidise it. On healthcare, the APC candidate promised to expand access to medical services by increasing the number of primary healthcare centres providing round-the-clock services. Hamzat said that out of the over 300 primary healthcare centres, the government planned to increase its flagship PHCs from 87 to 150, with the facilities operating 24 hours a day. He also disclosed that the state government was building more hospitals to improve healthcare access for residents. The post 2027 Elections: Lagos APC Candidate Hamzat Promises 4,000 CNG Buses, 77 Electric Ferries appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Seven killed, over 100 injured in Egypt train collision
item.description: At least seven people have been killed and more than 100 injured after two trains collided near Giza, Egypt, causing several carriages to derail and plunge down an embankment. The country’s railway authority said the trains, travelling south from Giza and Cairo, collided in the area between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Al-Ayyat. Egypt’s President, Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, said he had directed relevant authorities to investigate the circumstances surrounding the accident and ensure that anyone found negligent was held accountable. The public prosecutor’s office warned that the death toll could rise as rescue and recovery operations continued. The government said hospitals in the affected area had been placed on heightened alert to handle the large number of casualties. Health Minister, Dr Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, said victims were receiving treatment for various injuries, including broken bones and head injuries. The Egyptian Red Crescent also deployed personnel to provide emergency assistance and psychological support to victims and their families at the scene. The ministry confirmed that the driver of one of the trains was among those killed in the collision. According to reports, the first train was travelling from Giza to Fayoum when it crashed into the rear of another train heading from Cairo to Aswan, which was stationary on the tracks. Photographs from the scene showed several overturned carriages, with emergency responders and members of the public searching through the wreckage for survivors. Train services between Giza and the Upper Egypt region were suspended as cranes were deployed to remove the damaged trains. The railway authority had yet to announce when services would resume. The crash occurred close to the location of Egypt’s deadliest railway disaster, which happened in February 2002 when a fire engulfed a passenger train travelling from Cairo to Luxor, killing more than 370 people officially, although some estimates put the death toll higher. Two other train accidents in the area in 2009 also claimed dozens of lives. The latest disaster sparked calls on Sunday for Egypt’s transport minister to resign over the recurring railway accidents. Meanwhile, foreign governments and diplomatic representatives expressed condolences and solidarity with Egypt over the tragedy. Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed solidarity with Egypt and wished the injured a speedy recovery. Turkey’s Ambassador to Egypt also conveyed his condolences on X to the victims, their families and the Egyptian people. BBC The post Seven killed, over 100 injured in Egypt train collision appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Dalot’s muddled performances are just another symptom of Old Trafford chaos | Will Unwin
item.description: The stand-in left-back has become a pantomime villain but United fans are understandably struggling to focus their ire Sporting success is, supposedly, a nigh-on irrelevance to Manchester United’s global brand. The money will stream in regardless thanks to the behemoth company it has become, leaving behind its football club roots and becoming the world’s greatest soap opera creating the sort of drama of which Phil Mitchell can only dream. There is a strong cast of characters from the hated billionaire owners to the under‑pressure manager and pantomime villain Diogo Dalot, and a collection of storylines that are becoming hard to believe. Amid the supervillains, there are the unmistakable petty culprits who have brought United down to 18th place in the Premier League and Michael Carrick wondering how much longer he can survive. item.title: No Political Will To Deal With Agberos In Lagos, Says NDC’s Funsho Doherty
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Lagos State, Funsho Doherty, has blamed the persistence of the agbero system in the state on a lack of political will by successive administrations to reform the transport sector. Agberos are transport touts who collect money from commercial bus drivers and other transport operators at motor parks, bus stops and along roads, often claiming to represent transport unions or park authorities. Speaking during the Lagos Governorship Debate on Sunday, Doherty said powerful interests within the existing transport system had made it difficult for successive governments to tackle the activities of the operators. The debate was organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, a coalition of five media organisations: Channels Television, TVC News, The PUNCH, TheCable and Vanguard Newspapers. “Many of us understand this notion of the agbero system that people talk about. There is no political will to deal with that problem,” Doherty said. He argued that meaningful reform of public transportation would require a government that was accountable to residents rather than interests benefiting from the existing arrangement. “We will modernise the transportation system because we will be elected by the people, not by an agbero network,” he said.
