item.title: Idris inaugurates APC 2027 Campaign Council in Kebbi
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi Kebbi State Governor, Dr Nasir Idris, has inaugurated the All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 Campaign Council, charging members to work towards securing victory for all party candidates in the forthcoming general elections. The governor inaugurated the council on Sunday at the Presidential Lodge, Birnin Kebbi, urging members to demonstrate commitment, dedication and determination in discharging their responsibilities. He described Kebbi as an APC stronghold and called on party stakeholders to return to their respective communities to mobilise support for the party’s candidates across all elective positions. Idris announced former Kebbi State Governor and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Turkey, Ambassador Saidu Usman Nasamu Dakingari, as chairman of the campaign council. “I have the honour and privilege of inaugurating this campaign council for the 2027 General Elections, which will be headed by the former Governor of Kebbi State and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Turkey, His Excellency, Ambassador Saidu Usman Nasamu Dakingari. I wish all members the very best of luck,” the governor said. Speaking at the event, the APC State Chairman, Alhaji Abubakar Kana-Zuru, commended Idris for his support for the party and commitment to the successful inauguration of the campaign council. He urged members to remain dedicated to campaign activities, work collectively and ensure the party’s success in the forthcoming elections. In his response, Dakingari thanked the governor for the confidence reposed in him and other members of the council. He assured the governor that the committee would work diligently and collectively to achieve the party’s objectives. “On behalf of all members of the committee, I assure you that we are fully committed to delivering on this assignment. We will work hard and put in our best to ensure the success of the APC in the 2027 General Elections,” he said. The post Idris inaugurates APC 2027 Campaign Council in Kebbi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Police arrest six suspected phone thieves at Makinde’s Bauchi rally
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested six suspected phone thieves accused of stealing mobile phones from participants at the presidential campaign flag-off of the Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM) candidate, Governor Seyi Makinde, in the state. The suspects were arrested by operatives of the Police Violent Crimes Response Unit (VCRU), deployed to provide security at the campaign venue, following the detection of their suspicious movements during the event. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Nafiu Habib, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying exhibits were recovered from four of the suspects, while two others were identified by a victim as allegedly responsible for stealing his phone. The suspects were identified as Muhammad Rabiu, 20; Ibrahim Abubakar, 25; Hamza Usman, 18; Abba Bala, 20; Auwal Muhammad, 23; and Inusa Adamu, 20. Items recovered from them included an itel torchlight phone, an OPPO Android phone, an Infinix Smart 20 phone and a 20,000mAh power bank. The police spokesman said a Samsung Fold 4 allegedly stolen during the event had yet to be recovered, adding that efforts were being intensified to retrieve the device and other missing valuables. He said investigation was ongoing and that the suspects would be charged to court upon its conclusion. The Commissioner of Police, Sani-Omolori Aliyu, commended the operatives for their vigilance and prompt action, which led to the arrests and recovery of some stolen items. He warned criminal elements against exploiting public gatherings and political events to perpetrate crime, stressing that the command would not relent in its efforts to rid the state of criminal activities. The commissioner also urged members of the public attending political rallies and other public events to remain vigilant, safeguard their valuables and promptly report suspicious movements to security operatives. He called for continued public cooperation through the provision of timely and credible information to assist the command in preventing and controlling crime. The post Police arrest six suspected phone thieves at Makinde’s Bauchi rally appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Police rescue five kidnap victims, arrest three suspects in Kebbi
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has rescued five kidnapped victims and arrested three suspects following a coordinated security operation in Dakingari, Suru Local Government Area of the state. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman Kebbi, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying the operation followed credible intelligence that armed men had invaded Dolen Kwandage Village and abducted three residents. The victims were identified as Samaila Abubakar, 35; Dayyaba Muhammadu, 32; and Balki Hakimi, 31. According to the statement, police operatives, working in collaboration with local vigilantes, swiftly mobilised to the area and pursued the assailants. The police said the superior firepower of the security team forced the kidnappers to abandon their captives, leading to the rescue of the three newly abducted residents and two other women who had earlier been held in captivity. The two women were identified as Moe Muddaha, 50, and Hadiza Bello, 30, both from Yarma Village in Suru LGA. All five victims were rescued unhurt and taken to the General Hospital, Dakingari, for medical examination before being reunited with their families. The operation also led to the arrest of three suspects identified as Umaru Janyo, 49, and Bube Kwaire, 28, both from Bendu Village, and Muhammadu Gyade, 22, of Tindifai Village. The police said other members of the criminal gang escaped with suspected gunshot injuries. Items recovered during the operation included an unregistered Haojue motorcycle, ₦308,000 in cash, a chain and a jerrycan. The command said it had intensified security patrols and surveillance in the area, adding that efforts were ongoing to track down the fleeing suspects and bring all those involved to justice. The Commissioner of Police, CP Umar M. Hadejia, commended the operatives and their local vigilante collaborators for their prompt response, courage and effective coordination. He reiterated the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property, disrupting criminal networks and ensuring that perpetrators of violent crimes were brought to justice. Hadejia also urged members of the public to continue providing timely and credible information to security agencies to strengthen collective security efforts. The post Police rescue five kidnap victims, arrest three suspects in Kebbi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Makinde backs state police, vows security overhaul
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has backed the establishment of state police, pledging to decentralise Nigeria’s security architecture if elected president in the 2027 general elections. Makinde stated this on Sunday during a live political programme on Jay FM 101.9 in Jos, Plateau State, where he outlined his proposed security reforms ahead of the party’s presidential campaign activities in the city. “I believe that we need to decentralise our security architecture. State police is one of the ways to achieve this, but it must be properly structured. “States that are ready should be allowed to establish their own police formations, while others can come on board when they are prepared,” he said. Recalling his engagement with former President Muhammadu Buhari on the issue in 2019, Makinde said the former president had expressed concerns about the ability of some states to fund their police formations. “When we approached President Buhari in 2019, one of the concerns he raised was that some states could not even pay workers’ salaries. He questioned how such states would be able to fund state police,” he said. Explaining the alternative adopted by governors in the South-West, Makinde said they settled for a regional security arrangement through Amotekun. He said the operatives gather intelligence and work with federal security agencies, adding that the initiative had helped improve security coordination in the region. The APM presidential candidate acknowledged concerns that state police could be abused by governors to intimidate political opponents and other citizens, but insisted that appropriate safeguards could address such risks. “We must not pretend that there are no concerns. Some people are worried that governors could use state police to oppress their opponents or intimidate citizens. Those concerns are valid, and we must put safeguards in place. “But the fact that something can be abused does not mean we should not do it. We must design a system that ensures accountability and protects the rights of the people,” he said. On the pace of implementation, Makinde said states should be allowed to establish their police formations at different times, depending on their readiness and capacity. He cited Nigeria’s transition to self-government and independence as an example of how states could adopt the arrangement at different paces. “We had self-government in 1957 and independence in 1960. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has backed the establishment of state police, pledging to decentralise Nigeria’s security architecture if elected president in the 2027 general elections. Makinde stated this on Sunday during a live political programme on Jay FM 101.9 in Jos, Plateau State, where he outlined his proposed security reforms ahead of the party’s presidential campaign activities in the city. “I believe that we need to decentralise our security architecture. State police is one of the ways to achieve this, but it must be properly structured. “States that are ready should be allowed to establish their own police formations, while others can come on board when they are prepared,” he said. Recalling his engagement with former President Muhammadu Buhari on the issue in 2019, Makinde said the former president had expressed concerns about the ability of some states to fund their police formations. “When we approached President Buhari in 2019, one of the concerns he raised was that some states could not even pay workers’ salaries. He questioned how such states would be able to fund state police,” he said. Explaining the alternative adopted by governors in the South-West, Makinde said they settled for a regional security arrangement through Amotekun. He said the operatives gather intelligence and work with federal security agencies, adding that the initiative had helped improve security coordination in the region. The APM presidential candidate acknowledged concerns that state police could be abused by governors to intimidate political opponents and other citizens, but insisted that appropriate safeguards could address such risks. “We must not pretend that there are no concerns. Some people are worried that governors could use state police to oppress their opponents or intimidate citizens. Those concerns are valid, and we must put safeguards in place. “But the fact that something can be abused does not mean we should not do it. We must design a system that ensures accountability and protects the rights of the people,” he said. On the pace of implementation, Makinde said states should be allowed to establish their police formations at different times, depending on their readiness and capacity. He cited Nigeria’s transition to self-government and independence as an example of how states could adopt the arrangement at different paces. “We had self-government in 1957 and independence in 1960. We did not achieve everything at once. In the same way, states can move at different paces,” he said. Makinde also warned that Nigeria’s growing population, particularly its large youth population, required urgent government attention through job creation and opportunities for economic advancement. “We are talking about a country that could have a population of over 300 million people, with more than 70 per cent below the age of 34. We must create opportunities for these young people. “If we fail to provide pathways for them to succeed, we should not be surprised when some of them turn to crime or other activities that threaten the stability of the country,” he said. Beyond security, the governor said his proposed Reset Agenda would address the country’s economic and governance challenges, insisting that Nigeria needed fundamental changes rather than superficial adjustments. “When you talk about reform, it means that there is something good in the system that you want to improve upon. But when the bad outweighs the good, you need to take a different course of action. “If what you have in the system is only about 20 per cent of what you expected, you don’t need to continue tweaking it. You need to press the reset button, shut it down and reboot it. That is what Nigeria needs at this point,” he said. On the economy, Makinde said government policies should be assessed by their impact on the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians rather than economic statistics alone. “The economy must work for everybody. We should not just be talking about foreign reserves, World Bank figures or inflation statistics. What matters is whether ordinary Nigerians can afford to feed themselves and meet their basic needs. “If the people on the streets are not feeling any improvement, then we cannot say that the economy is doing well. The real test of economic performance is the condition of the people,” he said. He said his proposed administration would prioritise skills acquisition, entrepreneurship, education and production to create jobs and stimulate economic growth. “We must encourage our people to acquire skills and become entrepreneurs. We must invest in education and move towards intensive production. Government must provide an environment where businesses can thrive and young people can find meaningful employment,” he said. Explaining his decision to join politics, Makinde said he was motivated by concerns about the country’s future rather than a desire to pursue a career in politics. “I am not a career politician. I came into politics because I believe that the future of millions of Nigerians is at stake. We have the potential to become the greatest Black nation on the face of the earth, but we must make the right decisions to achieve that destiny,” he said. item.title: Lagos 2027: PDP’s Deji Doherty Defends Alliance With Wike, Tinubu
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Lagos State, Adedeji Doherty, has defended his political relationship with the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, despite the latter’s support for President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC). Doherty said Wike’s position in the APC-led Federal Government does not make him an enemy of democracy, arguing that politics and democracy can accommodate different political alignments. He spoke during the 2027 Lagos State governorship debate organised by Channels Television, TVC, Punch Newspapers, Vanguard Newspapers and The Cable on Sunday. Responding to a question on how he could offer a genuine opposition alternative in Lagos despite emerging from a PDP faction loyal to Wike, Doherty said his candidacy was the product of 26 years of political work and grassroots support. “My emergence in the People’s Democratic Party is out of 26 years of hard work, consistency, determination, and continued support for the grassroots. I have built a grassroots structure right from scratch, and I know there are a lot of people here that can testify to that. That’s number one. “Number two is that Nyesom Wike is our leader. He’s our national leader. He will continue to be my leader, and he will continue to show us that politics and democracy are not enemies,” he said. The PDP candidate further defended Wike’s relationship with the President, pointing to what he described as benefits from the Federal Government. “Once we are getting results from the FCT, we are getting results from Mr. President, we are getting monies into the pockets of governors in different states,” Doherty added. Watch the video below: ﻿ The post Lagos 2027: PDP’s Deji Doherty Defends Alliance With Wike, Tinubu appeared first on Channels Television .

The APC candidate said the priority should be to ensure that the drainage channels remain free of blockages so that water can flow into the creeks. Traffic: APC’s Multi-Modal Transportation Plan On traffic and transportation, Hamzat outlined the APC government’s plans to improve mobility through rail, road and water transportation. Obafemi Hamzat is the Deputy Governor of Lagos and the APC governorship candidate for the 2027 general elections. He said the state was targeting the movement of one million passengers daily through 4,000 compressed natural gas (CNG) buses. The deputy governor also disclosed plans to expand water transportation through 77 electric ferries, arguing that more commuters could be moved through the state’s waterways. Q: Do you agree with socila media comments that Lagos is smelly? Obafemi Hamzat: Lagos generates a lot of waste; enormous numbers of people come into Lagos . What is happening is that Lagos has a small landmass, and it is difficult to expand waste landfills. What is happening right now is that we are expanding from collection and dumping to collection and material recovery #LagosGovernorshipDebate #LagosDecides #NigeriaDebateConsortium — Channels Television (@channelstv) November 8, 2026 Defending the government’s investment in rail transportation, Hamzat said there was nowhere in Africa where the private sector had funded a rail system. However, the ADC candidate said traffic jams should not be a lifestyle. He disclosed that the improvement of water transportation and the provision for more infrastructure should be normalised. Housing: 100,000 Units, Mortgages, Rent Regulation Housing emerged as another area of competing priorities, with Rhodes-Vivour promising more than 100,000 housing units if elected. The ADC candidate said the units would be made accessible to residents, arguing that successive APC administrations had prioritised the interests of the elite over the needs of people in rural communities. He criticised the state’s emphasis on internally generated revenue (IGR), saying residents were not experiencing the benefits of the revenue generated. “Lagos celebrates high IGR, yet people are not experiencing it,” he said, adding that his administration would direct policies towards residents struggling with the cost of living. Hamzat, on his part, said the state had created 24 housing estates in the last eight years but acknowledged the need to expand access to quality accommodation. He promised to make more mortgage facilities available to residents and complete ongoing housing projects in different parts of Lagos. The APC candidate also pledged to enforce the Lagos State Real Estate Registration Agency Law, which mandates landlords to collect only one year’s rent rather than demand payment for multiple years. He said the government would ensure compliance with the law to address arbitrary rent demands and make accommodation more accessible. Education: NDC’s Doherty Promises ‘Truly Free’ Schooling On education, Doherty made one of the debate’s clearest social policy promises, pledging to make education completely free in Lagos if elected in 2027. The NDC candidate said his administration would prioritise equipping residents with education and relevant skills to improve their lives. Funsho Doherty is the NDC governorship candidate for the 2027 general elections. He argued that no child should be denied an education because their parents could not afford the cost, stressing that free education must go beyond the removal of tuition fees. “So, our policies are aimed at capacitating the people, giving them skills, ensuring that there is no child born in Lagos who does not get an education because their parents cannot afford it. “We have said we will make education truly free, not nominally free. Truly free, so people will not pay exam fees; they will not be asked to come and pay taxes at a point when they have to write their exams,” Doherty said. The problem (housing) that exists today was not created in one year. It is because housing supply has not kept up with growth in demand… -Funso Doherty, Lagos State Governorship Candidate, NDC, speaking on arbitrary rent increases in Lagos #LagosGovernorshipDebate #LagosDecides #NigeriaDebateConsortium — Channels Television (@channelstv) November 8, 2026 He also promised to introduce a programme that would provide children in public schools with one affordable meal every day. PDP Candidate Raises Concerns Over Lagos Debt Beyond transportation, housing and education, PDP candidate Deji Doherty raised concerns about the state’s debt profile, arguing that the cost of servicing its domestic and external debts was weighing down the economy. Deji Doherty is the PDP governorship candidate for the 2027 general elections. He said Lagos spends between ₦19 billion and ₦20 billion on debt servicing, describing the financial obligation as a significant burden on the state. “The debt burden (in Lagos) is heavy. When you are paying close to about 19 to 20 billion in external debt, in domestic debt, in foreign debt, then you have a burden you are carrying that is weighing you down,” he said. Doherty also criticised what he described as the lack of independence of local government areas, arguing that they were closest to the people and should have the resources to address their needs. “When your LGAs are not independent, those are the closest to the people, and when you do not give them what they need, when you are taking in LASAA and putting it in the pocket of the state, these are the issues,” he added. item.dc:creator: Ayobami
item.content:encoded: Governorship candidates of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), All Progressives Congress (APC), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) have presented their proposals for addressing some of Lagos State’s major challenges, including housing, transportation, and healthcare, ahead of the 2027 governorship election. The candidates made their positions known during the 2027 Lagos State governorship debate organised by Vanguard Channels Television, TVC, Punch Newspapers, and The Cable on Sunday. Housing The ADC candidate, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, promised to deliver more than 100,000 housing units if elected, saying his administration would prioritise affordable accommodation for ordinary residents rather than the wealthy. He said the proposed houses would be allocated transparently to prevent individuals from acquiring multiple units under the scheme. “The elites, the rich, can do it for themselves. The government’s role is to lift up people that cannot do it for themselves, and this comes into housing to ensure that we deliver 100,000-plus housing units and make it affordable so that it is transparently allocatable. We are not going to have a situation where one person can own ten units,” Rhodes-Vivour said. The ADC candidate also promised legislation to protect tenants against arbitrary rent increases, proposing that landlords should give at least six months’ notice before increasing rents, with the increment guided by a stipulated percentage. He added that a feedback mechanism would be established to enable tenants to report landlords who violated the proposed regulations, assuring that offenders would be brought to justice. The All Progressives Congress candidate, Obafemi Hamzat, who is the incumbent deputy governor, pledged to enforce existing regulations against arbitrary rent increases and the demand for multiple years’ rent in advance. Hamzat said his administration would ensure compliance with the Lagos State Real Estate Registration Agency Law, stressing that tenants should not be required to pay two or three years’ rent upfront. “The next chapter for Lagos is to enforce. To make sure people are not asked two or three years ahead, because people don’t get paid two or three years ahead,” he said. He also said the state had established 24 housing estates in the last eight years, promising to expand access to quality accommodation through increased mortgage facilities and the completion of ongoing housing projects across the state. The NDC candidate, Funsho Doherty, called for greater government involvement in providing affordable housing, arguing that private developers alone could not meet the accommodation needs of low- and middle-income residents. He also proposed the establishment of an ombudsman’s office to address what he described as exploitation of tenants through excessive agency, legal and other charges. Doherty said the housing shortage was largely driven by the failure of supply to keep pace with population growth and demand, particularly in the affordable and social housing segments. He argued that government should take the lead in addressing the gap rather than leaving housing provision largely to private investors. According to him, the last major government-led housing intervention in the state was during the administration of former Governor Lateef Jakande. Meanwhile, the PDP candidate, Adedeji Doherty, proposed that the Lagos State Government should become a major property developer and build houses which residents could rent directly from the government. He argued that government regulation alone could not force private landlords to reduce rents, insisting that the state should compete with them by providing more affordable accommodation. “There is no landlord, and there is no government that can control a landlord. What we are going to do is very simple. “We are going to rent those houses ourselves, and then you can come and rent from us if you want to,” he said. Doherty maintained that government must become the biggest housing developer in the state and provide alternatives to private rental accommodation. “If they cannot compete with the landlords, then let us forget it,” he said. Infrastructure On flooding and infrastructure, the candidates offered different approaches to managing Lagos State’s environmental challenges, with proposals ranging from improved drainage systems and wetland protection to climate adaptation, better road construction standards and infrastructure maintenance. The ADC candidate, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, said Lagos needed visionary leadership and modern engineering solutions to address flooding, particularly given its low-lying coastal geography. He cited cities such as Japan, Venice and the Netherlands as examples of places that had adopted innovative approaches to managing water, arguing that Lagos should learn from their experiences. Rhodes-Vivour criticised the practice of indiscriminate sand-filling of wetlands, saying alternative construction methods could allow water to flow naturally without worsening flooding. He cited the Makoko community as an example, arguing that building structures on concrete stilts could provide an alternative to filling wetlands. “There’s a technology there that they could have used, where we can build on concrete steels that still allow for water to flow,” he said. The ADC candidate also called for stricter standards for road construction, arguing that some newly constructed roads developed potholes shortly after the rainy season began. He also promised to protect wetlands from indiscriminate development, suggesting that such areas could be used for parks and solar farms. The All Progressives Congress candidate, Obafemi Hamzat, however, defended the state’s drainage infrastructure, describing it as extensive and stressing that its effectiveness depended largely on regular maintenance and preventing blockages. Hamzat, who IS a former commissioner for works and infrastructure, said Lagos faced significant environmental challenges because of its low-lying geography, heavy rainfall and large population. According to him, the priority should be ensuring that water moves freely through drainage channels into the creeks and lagoon. “Our going forward for us is to make sure that we maintain what we have built. Our climate change is real,” he said. Hamzat also defended the environmental assessment of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Road project, saying the assessment had been conducted when he was commissioner for works and infrastructure. He explained that the removal of structures from certain locations was necessary where buildings obstructed floodplains and the natural movement of water. The PDP candidate, Funsho Doherty, attributed Lagos’s flooding and environmental problems to what he described as years of governance failures, particularly the destruction of wetlands and development on drainage channels. He said the state’s coastal and low-lying geography required stronger environmental management to prevent residents from being exposed to avoidable flooding risks. Doherty described wetlands as natural systems that absorb excess water during rainfall, warning that destroying them and attempting to replace their functions with artificial drainage channels would not adequately address the problem. He also criticised the practice of allowing buildings to spring up on drainage channels before demolishing them years later, arguing that proper planning and enforcement would prevent such situations. The PDP candidate further faulted the Lagos State Government for what he described as its failure to insist on an environmental impact assessment before construction began on the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Road. Although the project is being undertaken by the Federal Government, he argued that the state government had a responsibility to protect its residents and ensure that environmental concerns were addressed. item.title: ‘That’s not going to happen’ – Carrick rules out resigning as Man United boss
item.description: Michael Carrick said he expects to “move forward and keep working” as Manchester United manager despite dropping into the Premier League relegation zone. United twice came from two goals down to salvage a remarkable 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday. Goals in stoppage time from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu rescued a point and potentially gave Carrick a stay of execution ahead of a two-week international break. “We haven’t won enough games, but I expect to move forward and keep working on the things that we’ve been working on,” Carrick told Sky Sports. “Showing a lot of the good (things) in the game today, tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches.” Results this weekend dropped United into the bottom three after August for the first time in 40 years. “We’re in November,” added Carrick. “I don’t like the situation where we are, I don’t like the results that we’ve had, but we can definitely do something about it.” The former United midfielder dismissed any suggestion he could resign if it was in the best interests of the club and said he would not seek out discussions with his superiors on where his future lies. “That’s not going to happen,” said Carrick when asked if he would resign. “I’m quite clear what direction the club needs to go in, and we’ve just got to win games.” The 45-year-old added: “I’m pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there… as a normal international week is, we’ll have some training, we’ll have one or two days off, not too much, but we’ll train and get ready for the next game.” United travel to rivals Liverpool when they are next in action on November 22. Vanguard News The post ‘That’s not going to happen’ – Carrick rules out resigning as Man United boss appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Scottish roundup: flying Falkirk hit five to shatter Hearts’ long unbeaten home run
item.description: Falkirk leapfrog their hosts with 5-2 rout at Tynecastle Liam Scales gives Celtic 1-0 home win over Kilmarnock Falkirk obliterated Hearts ’ 18-month unbeaten home record in the Scottish Premiership with a stunning 5-2 win at Tynecastle on Sunday as they leapfrogged their hosts into third place. Wouter Vrancken’s beleaguered side, missing 11 players through injury, were in disarray as Falkirk romped into a five-goal lead early in the second half through Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell’s double. Hearts hit back through Sabri Guendouz, on as a substitute, and a Cláudio Braga penalty, but Falkirk were well worthy of making it five top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1995. item.title: Debate: ‘Agbero interests holding back Lagos public transport’ – NDC’s Doherty
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Lagos State, Funso Doherty, has accused vested interests within the state’s informal transport network of frustrating efforts to modernise public transportation. Doherty made the remarks during the Lagos governorship debate in Lagos on Friday organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium comprising Channels Television, TVC News, The PUNCH, TheCable and Vanguard, where he criticised the continued reliance on ageing commercial buses and the influence of the agbero system in the state’s transport sector. He questioned why successive administrations had failed to modernise public transportation despite the thousands of rickety buses operating across Lagos. “Our public transportation system is not modernised. Thousands of rickety buses are moving around. We must ask ourselves: are these what our people deserve? Why has it taken so long to modernise public transportation?” he asked. The NDC candidate argued that the failure to reform the system was not accidental, alleging that powerful interests benefited from the existing arrangement. “In my opinion, the lack of modern transportation is not by accident. There are vested interests in operating the bus system the way it is. Many of us understand the agbero system; there is an ecosystem around it, and there is no political will to deal with that problem,” he said. Doherty, who promised to overhaul the state’s public transportation system if elected, said his administration would not be beholden to informal transport networks. “We would modernise public transportation because we would be elected by the people and not by the agbero network,” he added. Vanguard News The post Debate: ‘Agbero interests holding back Lagos public transport’ – NDC’s Doherty appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Nigeria needs reset, not reforms — Makinde
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has said Nigeria needs a fundamental reset rather than mere reforms to address its economic, security and governance challenges ahead of the 2027 general elections. Makinde spoke on Sunday during a live political programme on Jay FM 101.9 in Jos, Plateau State, ahead of the party’s presidential campaign flag-off scheduled for Monday in the city. Explaining his position, the governor argued that reforms were insufficient where the problems in a system outweighed its strengths. “When you talk about reform, it means that there is something good in the system that you want to improve upon. But when the bad outweighs the good, you need to take a different course of action. “If what you have in the system is only about 20 per cent of what you expected, you don’t need to continue tweaking it. You need to press the reset button, shut it down and reboot it. That is what Nigeria needs at this point. Reform will not work in the present environment,” he said. The governor said he did not initially intend to become a politician but was motivated by concerns about the country’s future. “I am not a career politician. I came into politics because I believe that the future of millions of Nigerians is at stake. We have the potential to become the greatest Black nation on the face of the earth, but we must make the right decisions to achieve that destiny,” he said. On the economy, Makinde identified it as the foremost priority of his proposed Reset Agenda, arguing that economic performance should be measured by improvements in the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians. “The economy must work for everybody. We should not just be talking about foreign reserves, World Bank figures or inflation statistics. What matters is whether ordinary Nigerians can afford to feed themselves and meet their basic needs,” he said. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has said Nigeria needs a fundamental reset rather than mere reforms to address its economic, security and governance challenges ahead of the 2027 general elections. Makinde spoke on Sunday during a live political programme on Jay FM 101.9 in Jos, Plateau State, ahead of the party’s presidential campaign flag-off scheduled for Monday in the city. Explaining his position, the governor argued that reforms were insufficient where the problems in a system outweighed its strengths. “When you talk about reform, it means that there is something good in the system that you want to improve upon. But when the bad outweighs the good, you need to take a different course of action. “If what you have in the system is only about 20 per cent of what you expected, you don’t need to continue tweaking it. You need to press the reset button, shut it down and reboot it. That is what Nigeria needs at this point. Reform will not work in the present environment,” he said. The governor said he did not initially intend to become a politician but was motivated by concerns about the country’s future. “I am not a career politician. I came into politics because I believe that the future of millions of Nigerians is at stake. We have the potential to become the greatest Black nation on the face of the earth, but we must make the right decisions to achieve that destiny,” he said. On the economy, Makinde identified it as the foremost priority of his proposed Reset Agenda, arguing that economic performance should be measured by improvements in the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians. “The economy must work for everybody. We should not just be talking about foreign reserves, World Bank figures or inflation statistics. What matters is whether ordinary Nigerians can afford to feed themselves and meet their basic needs,” he said. He added that economic progress should be assessed by its impact on households rather than statistical indicators alone. “If the people on the streets are not feeling any improvement, then we cannot say that the economy is doing well. The real test of economic performance is the condition of the people,” he said. The APM candidate said his proposed administration would prioritise skills acquisition, entrepreneurship, education and production, while creating an enabling environment for businesses to grow and generate employment. “We must encourage our people to acquire skills and become entrepreneurs. We must invest in education and move towards intensive production. Government must provide an environment where businesses can thrive and young people can find meaningful employment,” he said. On insecurity, Makinde advocated decentralising Nigeria’s security architecture through the establishment of state police, arguing that states should be allowed to adopt the arrangement when they are ready and necessary safeguards are in place. “I believe that we need to decentralise our security architecture. State police is one of the ways to achieve this, but it must be properly structured. States that are ready should be allowed to establish their own police formations, while others can come on board when they are prepared,” he said. Recalling his engagement with former President Muhammadu Buhari on the issue in 2019, Makinde said the former president had expressed concerns about the ability of some states to finance their own police formations. “When we approached President Buhari in 2019, one of the concerns he raised was that some states could not even pay workers’ salaries. He questioned how such states would be able to fund state police,” he said. He explained that governors in the South-West subsequently adopted the Western Nigeria Security Network, popularly known as Amotekun, as an alternative arrangement to strengthen security in the region. “We decided to find a middle ground through Amotekun. The operatives gather intelligence and work with the federal security agencies. It has helped to improve security coordination in the region,” he said. Makinde acknowledged concerns that state police could be abused by governors to intimidate political opponents and ordinary citizens but insisted that appropriate safeguards could address such risks. “We must not pretend that there are no concerns. Some people are worried that governors could use state police to oppress their opponents or intimidate citizens. Those concerns are valid, and we must put safeguards in place. “But the fact that something can be abused does not mean we should not do it. We must design a system that ensures accountability and protects the rights of the people,” he said. On Nigeria’s growing population, the governor warned that failure to provide opportunities for young people could worsen insecurity and social instability. He said the country could have a population of more than 300 million, with over 70 per cent below the age of 34, stressing the need to create opportunities for the youthful population. “If we fail to provide pathways for them to succeed, we should not be surprised when some of them turn to crime or other activities that threaten the stability of the country,” he said. Makinde also cited Nigeria’s gradual transition to self-government and independence as an example of how different parts of the country could adopt new arrangements at different times. “We had self-government in 1957 and independence in 1960. We did not achieve everything at once. In the same way, states do not necessarily have to establish state police at the same time. Those that are ready can begin, provided the necessary safeguards are in place,” he said. Recalling his handling of the COVID-19 lockdown in Oyo State in 2020, the governor said he opposed a blanket shutdown because of the hardship it could impose on residents who depended on daily earnings for survival. “I remember that during COVID-19, there was a proposal for a mandatory lockdown. I raised the concern that many people depended on what they earned each day to feed their families. If you locked them down completely, what would they eat that night or the following morning?” he said. He maintained that decisions on public health and governance should be guided by science, data and logic, while taking into account the realities of ordinary citizens. “We had to look at the situation and make decisions based on science, data and logic. We also had to understand the realities of our people. Some people were more worried about dying of hunger than the risk of contracting COVID-19,” he said. On education, Makinde praised the legacy of the late nationalist and statesman, Chief Obafemi Awolowo, particularly his free education policy, which he said expanded opportunities for generations of Nigerians. “Chief Awolowo understood that education was an investment in the future. The cocoa farmers paid their taxes, and the government used the resources to provide free education for children. “Those children grew up, became professionals and contributed to society. That is the kind of investment we must make in our people,” he said. The governor said his proposed administration would also prioritise honesty, transparency and accountability in the management of public resources. “The first thing I will do is to tell Nigerians the truth about the state of the country. People deserve to know where we are and what needs to be done. “The next thing is accountability. If you have accountability, then the chances are that public resources will be used for the benefit of the people,” he said. item.title: Customs processes 99,839 cargo declarations in two months
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) processed 9,195 Pre-Arrival Assessment Reports (PAARs) and 99,839 Single Goods Declarations (SGDs) between September and October 2026, generating a combined revenue of approximately ₦1.42 trillion. The figures were disclosed during a joint security press briefing at the National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC), under the Office of the National Security Adviser, in Abuja. Speaking at the briefing, the National Public Relations Officer of the NCS, Deputy Comptroller Abdullahi Aliyu Maiwada, said the performance reflected the Service’s commitment to facilitating legitimate trade, improving cargo clearance and strengthening revenue generation through digital interventions and collaboration with stakeholders. A breakdown of the figures showed that the Service processed 2,102 PAARs in September and 7,093 in October, bringing the total to 9,195. Similarly, 48,832 SGDs were processed in September, while 51,007 were recorded in October, giving a combined total of 99,839 declarations. The Service collected ₦697.8 billion in revenue in September and ₦722.9 billion in October, amounting to ₦1.4207 trillion during the two-month period. In a statement, Maiwada also disclosed that the Service recorded significant progress in export trade facilitation. At the Lilypond Export Command, export activities in the third quarter of 2026 generated a total export value of $752.85 million, compared with $586.15 million recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. The statement put the increase at approximately 28.44 per cent, reflecting the growing contribution of the export sector and the impact of measures aimed at facilitating non-oil exports. On enforcement, the NCS said it seized prohibited and restricted items with a combined Duty Paid Value exceeding ₦8.1 billion during the period under review. The interceptions covered various categories, including illicit drugs, pharmaceutical products, prohibited goods and petroleum products. The Service said it continued to collaborate with relevant regulatory and security agencies to ensure the appropriate handling and disposition of seized items. On its anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) responsibilities, the NCS highlighted the ongoing World Customs Organisation (WCO) Mentoring Mission, inaugurated on October 19, 2026. The four-week engagement, scheduled to run from October 18 to November 13, 2026, is designed to strengthen the capacity of the Service to identify, investigate and tackle trade-based money laundering and other illicit financial activities associated with cross-border trade. As part of the exercise, the NCS engaged six relevant agencies between October 27 and 29, including the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), the Nigeria Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU) and the National Counter Terrorism Centre. Similarly, 48,832 SGDs were processed in September, while 51,007 were recorded in October, giving a combined total of 99,839 declarations. The Service collected ₦697.8 billion in revenue in September and ₦722.9 billion in October, amounting to ₦1.4207 trillion during the two-month period. In a statement, Maiwada also disclosed that the Service recorded significant progress in export trade facilitation. At the Lilypond Export Command, export activities in the third quarter of 2026 generated a total export value of $752.85 million, compared with $586.15 million recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. The statement put the increase at approximately 28.44 per cent, reflecting the growing contribution of the export sector and the impact of measures aimed at facilitating non-oil exports. On enforcement, the NCS said it seized prohibited and restricted items with a combined Duty Paid Value exceeding ₦8.1 billion during the period under review. The interceptions covered various categories, including illicit drugs, pharmaceutical products, prohibited goods and petroleum products. The Service said it continued to collaborate with relevant regulatory and security agencies to ensure the appropriate handling and disposition of seized items. On its anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) responsibilities, the NCS highlighted the ongoing World Customs Organisation (WCO) Mentoring Mission, inaugurated on October 19, 2026. The four-week engagement, scheduled to run from October 18 to November 13, 2026, is designed to strengthen the capacity of the Service to identify, investigate and tackle trade-based money laundering and other illicit financial activities associated with cross-border trade. As part of the exercise, the NCS engaged six relevant agencies between October 27 and 29, including the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), the Nigeria Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU) and the National Counter Terrorism Centre. The Service also disclosed that it had transitioned to an electronic currency declaration platform as part of efforts to improve transparency, strengthen monitoring and enhance the detection of illicit financial flows across the country’s borders. In another development, the NCS said six live pangolins were rescued in separate operations in Ogun State during the period. Three were rescued by the Ogun I Area Command, while another three were intercepted by the Federal Operations Unit, Zone A. The animals were subsequently handed over to the Green Fingers Wildlife Conservation Initiative for care and rehabilitation in line with Nigeria’s obligations under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES). item.title: VIDEO: Lagos Debt Burden Weighing State Down, Says PDP’s Deji Doherty
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Lagos State, Adedeji Doherty, has criticised the state’s debt burden, saying it is weighing down the economy. Doherty said this during the 2027 Lagos State governorship debate organised by Channels Television, TVC, Punch Newspapers, Vanguard Newspapers and The Cable on Sunday. He said Lagos spends close to 19 billion to 20 billion on servicing its external and domestic debts, describing the burden as heavy. “The debt burden (in Lagos) is heavy. When you are paying close to about 19 to 20 billion in external debt, in domestic debt, in foreign debt then you have a burden you are carrying that is weighing you down,” he said. The PDP candidate also faulted what he described as the lack of independence of local government areas, arguing that they are closest to the people and should have the resources to meet their needs. “When your LGAs are not independent, those are the closest to the people and when you do not give them what they need, when you are taking in LASAA and putting it in the pocket of the state, these are the issues,” he added. ﻿ The post VIDEO: Lagos Debt Burden Weighing State Down, Says PDP’s Deji Doherty appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 2027: We Will Make Education Truly Free In Lagos – NDC’s Funsho Doherty
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Funsho Doherty, has promised to make education completely free in Lagos State if elected in 2027. Doherty made the promise during the 2027 Lagos State governorship debate organised by Channels Television, TVC, Punch Newspapers, Vanguard Newspapers and The Cable on Sunday. He said his administration would focus on improving the lives of residents by equipping them with education and relevant skills. “So, our policies are aimed at capacitating the people, giving them skills, ensuring that there is no child born in Lagos who does not get an education because their parents cannot afford it. We have said we will make education truly free, not nominally free. Truly free, so people will not pay exam fees, they will not be asked to come and pay taxes at a point when they have to write their exams,” Doherty said. He also promised to introduce a programme that would provide children in public schools with one affordable meal every day. Watch the video below: ﻿ The post 2027: We Will Make Education Truly Free In Lagos – NDC’s Funsho Doherty appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Elvis and Eminem rights holders are suing Suno
item.description: Suno is facing yet another pair of lawsuits . A group of rights holders of Elvis Presley's music and the publisher of some of Eminem's biggest records are suing the AI music company, claiming it illegally generates music and lyrics that mimic those artists. The lawyers in the Presley suit claim that Suno has violated Tennessee's Ensuring Likeness Voice and Image Security (ELVIS) Act, which makes it illegal for an AI company to clone a singer's voice. In the suit, lawyers representing Presley's rights holders argue that "Suno has mechanically encoded itself with artists' identities, hard-work, creativity, and time, and harnessed them all for … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Gadi Eisenkot receives mandate to form government
item.description: Israel's opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has officially been tasked with forming the country's next government, following a formal announcement by President Isaac Herzog. He now has up to six weeks to negotiate with potential coalition partners and secure a parliamentary majority. While an alliance with Arab Israeli parties appears to be the easiest option mathematically, it remains politically sensitive. Eisenkot must now navigate difficult negotiations to build a coalition capable of replacing Benjamin Netanyahu. Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

item.title: Diego Gómez hits another stunner as Brighton beat 10-man Brentford to go second
item.description: Who can stop Brighton’s ­ascension in English and European football? They are setting standards, ­practices ­leaving almost everybody else ­trailing in their wake. A ­second‑place position in the ­Premier League would once have read like a glitch in a ­Football ­Manager ­session. Not in November 2026, where they appear the only team capable of throwing down any sort of challenge to Arsenal. Under low winter sun, Brentford, an opposition to which Brighton are often, if lazily, compared, were ­swatted aside. If Keith Andrews’s team, and their fans at the Amex ­Stadium, could level blame at a couple of ­refereeing decisions, they received little chance of rescuing anything. Brighton squeezed them, toyed with them. Continue reading...

item.description: A lot can change in five‑and‑a‑half months, but as an early winter chill descended on Wearside last week – both meteorologically and ­metaphorically – Sunderland were determined that some things should remain the same. Just as they had beaten Chelsea on the final day of last season to ensure European qualification for the first time in 53 years, they did so again on Sunday to lift themselves off the bottom of the Premier League. The Sunderland performance was certainly familiar to their head coach, Régis Le Bris – “the identity, the intensity, the togetherness, the way we managed the game” – on the way to three crucial points. item.title: Apple’s M5 MacBook Air is down to its lowest price since July
item.description: A top-down view of the 15-inch MacBook Air, which features Apple’s M5 processor. | Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge The latest 13-inch MacBook Air is currently available for $1,099.99, marking the second time we’ve seen this $200 discount following the company’s hefty price increases over the summer . Although the base model — which features Apple’s M5 processor, 16GB of RAM, and 512GB of storage — often sold for around $950 to $1,000 shortly after it launched in May, savings have been rare since July, making the current deal worth flagging. Amazon , Best Buy , and B&H Photo are all honoring the price across all color options. If you’d prefer something with a larger screen, a six-speaker array instead of four, and slightly more power (with two additional GPU cores in the M5), Apple’s 15-inch MacBook Air is also on sale for $200 off. Amazon , Best Buy , and B&H Photo are each selling the 16GB RAM / 512GB SSD configuration in most colors for $1,299.99. Apple 13-inch MacBook Air (M5) Where to Buy: $1299 $1099 at Amazon $1299 $1099 at Best Buy $1299 $1099 at B&H Photo Although it’s pricier than the newer MacBook Neo, the Air offers better value in numerous ways. It’s an ideal choice if you want faster performance, as it offers double the RAM and a speedier CPU with more cores. You also get twice as much storage, better speakers, a backlit keyboard, and a larger, higher-resolution screen. Given said differences, it’s easy to see how the Air’s improvements might make it worth the extra cost for some people. If you’re still on the fence, though, I’d recommend reading my colleague Antonio G. Di Benedetto’s reviews, both of which were published before the summer price increases. Read our full MacBook Neo and M5 MacBook Air reviews.

item.title: Legendary sci-fi magazine 'Starlog' returns as a yearly release, just in time for its 50th anniversary
item.description: null "Starlog" was one of the greatest sci-fi and fantasy magazines ever, and after a 17-year absence, it's being resurrected. The legendary sci-fi mag went dark back in 2009 as part of the wave of popular publications folding due to years of declining readership and subscriptions. But as of Nov. 13, this geek favorite periodical returns as an annual print edition, and it's available for pre-order now. It’s another indication of digital fatigue in the world, and fans of a certain age will recall the pleasure of poring over each colorful issue packed with in-depth interviews, behind-the-scenes photos, TV guides, classic movie retrospectives, book reviews, con news, and VFX features. The triumphant relaunch of "Starlog" magazine happens on Nov. 13, 2026 (Image credit: Fangoria Holdings) "Starlog" launched in 1976, in the pre-" Star Wars " days, under the leadership of editor-in-chief Kerry O’Quinn. It first arrived with artist Jack Thurston's beautiful painted "Star Trek" cover, featuring William Shatner as Captain James T. Kirk and Leonard Nimoy’s Spock, set against the U.S.S. Enterprise near a shimmering black hole. The magazine continued to inform the science fiction community about upcoming sci-fi TV shows and blockbuster Hollywood films for over three decades; I fondly recall reading each informative and entertaining monthly issue cover-to-cover. Just in time to honor its 50th anniversary this year, "Starlog" blasts back into the sci-fi universe with Issue #375 showcasing cover artwork created by Armenian artist Gabriel Yeganyan. Its geek culture legacy, covering iconic franchises like "Star Wars," "Star Trek," and "Alien," will now live on thanks to Fangoria Holdings and io9 co-founder Annalee Newitz, editor-in-chief. Three vintage "Starlog" magazine issues from my personal collection! (Image credit: Jeff Spry) "During its original 33-year run, 'Starlog' documented science fiction as it evolved across film, television, books, technology, and culture," said 'Fangoria's Tara Ansley. "Fifty years after the magazine first launched, the line between science fiction and the real world has become increasingly difficult to separate. That makes this an especially interesting time to bring 'Starlog' back. Technology may change, but the most compelling questions have always been about people: how we live, what we create, and what kind of future we want to build." "Starlog" reloads for its first annual edition after a long hiatus on Nov. 13. You can pre-order the first issue (Issue 375 in continuity) on the Starlog website .

It first arrived with artist Jack Thurston's beautiful painted "Star Trek" cover, featuring William Shatner as Captain James T. Kirk and Leonard Nimoy’s Spock, set against the U.S.S. Enterprise near a shimmering black hole. The magazine continued to inform the science fiction community about upcoming sci-fi TV shows and blockbuster Hollywood films for over three decades; I fondly recall reading each informative and entertaining monthly issue cover-to-cover. Just in time to honor its 50th anniversary this year, "Starlog" blasts back into the sci-fi universe with Issue #375 showcasing cover artwork created by Armenian artist Gabriel Yeganyan. Its geek culture legacy, covering iconic franchises like "Star Wars," "Star Trek," and "Alien," will now live on thanks to Fangoria Holdings and io9 co-founder Annalee Newitz, editor-in-chief. Three vintage "Starlog" magazine issues from my personal collection! (Image credit: Jeff Spry) "During its original 33-year run, 'Starlog' documented science fiction as it evolved across film, television, books, technology, and culture," said 'Fangoria's Tara Ansley. "Fifty years after the magazine first launched, the line between science fiction and the real world has become increasingly difficult to separate. That makes this an especially interesting time to bring 'Starlog' back. Technology may change, but the most compelling questions have always been about people: how we live, what we create, and what kind of future we want to build." "Starlog" reloads for its first annual edition after a long hiatus on Nov. 13. You can pre-order the first issue (Issue 375 in continuity) on the Starlog website .

item.title: NASA Announces $1 Million to Students for Moon Base Challenge
item.description: Artist’s concept depicting astronauts, habitats, rovers, power systems, and cargo operations supporting sustained human activities at the Moon Base near the lunar South Pole. Credit: NASA On Sunday, NASA announced the opening of its $1 million Moon Base Student Challenge during a MAX POWER event at Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Florida. As part of a Golden Age of Science, the competition invites student teams at U.S. high schools and post-secondary schools to contribute designs for the Moon Base. “We’re looking for students ready to think creatively, work as a team, and take on real problems connected to NASA’s future on the Moon,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “You do not have to wait until graduation to contribute. Curiosity, creativity, and the willingness to tackle hard problems without obvious answers are exactly the qualities we need as we build what comes next.” NASA is building a Moon Base where astronauts will live, work, and explore at the lunar South Pole region. A permanent human presence on the Moon paves the way for future crewed missions to Mars and requires talent from various industries and backgrounds. “As we build and design the foundations of Moon Base, we want to leverage all the ingenuity and innovation to think of every consideration our explorers might need to live and work there,” said Carlos García-Galán, manager, Moon Base Program. “Students bring exactly the bold ideas that we’re looking for, and I’m looking forward to their fresh perspective. Ultimately, Moon Base is for them, people who will experience a world where humans are on the Moon to stay.” The multiphase challenge supports NASA’s commitment to cultivating the technical skills of tomorrow’s aerospace workforce. For this challenge, student teams will design innovative solutions for Moon Base across six categories: power generation and storage, construction, life-support systems, surface mobility, communications networks, and astronaut safety. The challenge gives participants an opportunity to develop necessary skills for careers in the space industry while helping advance new concepts for Moon Base technologies. Participants are required to register for the challenge through the NASA STEM Gateway. Registration is open until Jan. 25, 2027. “Students are the next generation of explorers and innovators. Their unique perspectives are key to helping us envision a future away from Earth, and I’m excited to see the creativity and ingenuity spurred by this challenge,” said Elaine Ho, associate administrator for the Office of STEM Engagement at NASA Headquarters. The Moon Base Student Challenge addresses authentic environmental and mission design parameters for life and operations on the lunar surface. Their unique perspectives are key to helping us envision a future away from Earth, and I’m excited to see the creativity and ingenuity spurred by this challenge,” said Elaine Ho, associate administrator for the Office of STEM Engagement at NASA Headquarters. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 8, 2005: Europe launches Venus Express, its first mission to Venus
item.description: null On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. The spacecraft was called Venus Express. Venus is a hothouse planet, one where the atmospheric pressure can easily crush an unprotected spacecraft. Even from orbit, Venus Express had to survive harsh radiation. But the spacecraft lasted for more than nine years. During that time, Venus Express saw a weird vortex swirling around Venus's south pole . It also saw possible signs of active volcanoes . Venus Express also discovered that the planet generates its own auroras . These auroras happen when particles from the sun hit charged particles in the atmosphere. Late in the Venus Express mission, controllers told the spacecraft to dip down into Venus's clouds — even though the spacecraft wasn't designed to do this. It performed well, but eventually it stopped listening to commands. The spacecraft burned up in the atmosphere in January 2015. A Russian Soyuz rocket launches the Venus Express spacecraft to Venus on Nov. 8, 2005.. (Image credit: ESA) Why it mattered Venus Express established ESA as the third world organization to successfully send a probe to study Venus, following the United States and Soviet Union. (Japan's JAXA became the fourth five years later.) "By studying Venus, scientists learn how Earth-like planets change over time," reads a summary of the planet's exploration prepared by The Planetary Society. "Orbital studies [like Venus Express] hint that Venus may have hosted habitable oceans before becoming inhospitable." "By studying Venus, we can learn how Earth-like planets evolve and what shapes planets throughout the galaxy into temperate, lush worlds instead of sweltering hothouses. Venus also helps scientists model Earth’s climate, and may serve as a cautionary tale on how dramatically a planet’s climate can change," wrote the Society. An illustration of the Venus Express spacecraft in orbit around Venus. (Image credit: ESA) ESA returned to Venus in 2018 when BepiColombo, its joint mission with JAXA, used the planet's gravity to redirect its path toward the planet Mercury. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Chatbots might be coming to Apple’s HomeView
item.description: Code in the iOS 27.3 beta suggests that Apple could add support for chatbots to its smart home hub. There's a flag listed for a "Conversational Apps" category. While there are no details about what apps would fall under that heading, it seems reasonable that AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude could be added to HomeView. According to pdfu on X, that new beta also adds support for bidirectional audio routing and session management, but says it's "still not fully wired up." Apple has also added anti-spoofing protection that will require a user to authenticate themselves with an iPhone after three failed attempts. It will also have a lockout s … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: US voters reject AI data centres: could the backlash spread to France?
item.description: In Tuesday’s US midterm elections, voters weighed in on more than 40 local measures on data centres, and sided against them in all but one. With Democrats taking control of Congress in January and new governors in Texas and Georgia calling for moratoriums, the AI building boom faces its toughest political test yet.

item.title: Yemen's humanitarian crisis worsens
item.description: One month into the Yemeni government's offensive against the Iran-aligned Houthis, fighting continues to escalate along the Red Sea coast. Rula Amin, Senior Communications Advisor and spokesperson at UNHCR at Amman, in Jordan, shares further details.

item.title: Poland in shock after 6 killed in Krakow far-right shooting
item.description: Poland on Sunday launched a terror probe into the mass shooting in Krakow the day before, in which six people were killed and many more were injured. Authorities have said that the 24-year-old suspect, who used a semi-automatic rifle in his killing spree, was “fascinated by far-right ideologies”. He is currently in critical condition in hospital. FRANCE 24 journalist Adrien Sariat reports from Poland.

item.title: Russo on target again as double fires under-pressure Arsenal to vital WSL win at Liverpool
item.description: If a good striker can always get their team out of a hole, Alessia Russo is doing her best to drag Arsenal out of a deep chasm of uncertainty. Her two goals gave the ­under‑pressure Arsenal head coach, Renée Slegers, some brief respite with a much-needed, albeit still rather unconvincing victory. Russo’s double took her impressive recent tally to seven goals in her past four appearances. Her goals were priceless for an Arsenal team who arrived on Merseyside with just one win in their previous seven Women’s Super League games. They will be relieved to have won after Liverpool posed plenty of problems and the hosts were unhappy about a ­disallowed goal. Continue reading...

item.title: Who is King Ghidorah? The cosmic connections of Godzilla Minus Zero's foe
item.description: null Godzilla goes toe-to-toe with long-time foe King Ghidorah in Godzilla Minus Zero, which opened in theaters on Friday (Nov. 6). Though the three-headed golden Kaiju might seem like a natural native of Monster Island, King Ghidorah actually emerged from the depths of space. However, it isn't just the origins of King Ghidorah — also known as Monster Zero in the Godzilla movie Invasion of Astro-Monster (1965) — that are this beast's only cosmic connection. One of the largest structures in the universe, the King Ghidorah Supercluster , was named in honor of Godzilla's primary antagonist. Eat that, King Kong! King Ghidorah and Godzilla The three heads of King Ghidorah seen in Godzilla Minus Zero (Image credit: Toho Studios) King Ghidorah is a three-headed, twin-tailed golden dragon from the stars, first introduced in the fifth Godzilla movie, Ghidorah, the Three-Headed Monster (1964). In this first appearance, part of the Shōwa era (1964–1975) of Godzilla history, Ghidorah ravaged Venus , wiping out its population 5,000 years before arriving on Earth encased within a highly magnetic meteorite . Ghidorah was bested this first time by Godzilla, Rodan, and Mothra. Undeterred, Ghidorah returned for a rematch just a year later in Invasion of Astro Monster (1965), after being discovered supposedly terrorizing the inhabitants of Planet X, a world found beyond Jupiter . In this movie, it is revealed that Ghidorah is less a king and more a pawn, under the control of calculating Xiliens as part of a plan to subjugate Earth. This will become a theme. King Ghidorah flying and blasting lightning from its three mouths in Invasion of Astro Monster (1965). (Image credit: Toho Studios) Freed from that control, Ghidorah returns to deep space, once again falling under the thrall of an alien race in 1968's Destroy All Monsters. This movie sees Ghidorah hold its own against a who's who of kaiju, eventually succumbing to the combined might of Godzilla, Minilla, Mothra, Rodan, Manda, Gorosaurus, Anguirus, Kumonga, Baragon, and Varan. Even with three gravity-beam-blasting heads, that is hardly fair! Ghidorah returned with some backup for a final time in the Shōwa era in 1975's Godzilla vs. Gigan. This time, Ghidorah and his tag-team partner Gigan (who resembled a giant one-eyed space chicken) were under the control of cockroach-like Nebulans. Getting mind-controlled three times is just embarrassing! Fortunately, the Shōwa era drew to a close in 1975 before Ghidorah was forced into servitude for a fourth time. Mecha-King Ghidorah battling Godzilla in Godzilla Vs. King Ghidorah (1991). (Image credit: Tohu Pictures) Ghidorah returned in the rebooted Godzilla timeline of the Heisei era (1991–1998) in 1991's Godzilla Vs. King Ghidorah, but its cosmic origins are gone. The Heisei Ghidorah begins life as three genetically engineered creatures called Dorats in the future before being morphed into a three-headed form via nuclear exposure. Ghidorah was given a spiritual origin in

King Ghidorah flying and blasting lightning from its three mouths in Invasion of Astro Monster (1965). (Image credit: Toho Studios) Freed from that control, Ghidorah returns to deep space, once again falling under the thrall of an alien race in 1968's Destroy All Monsters. This movie sees Ghidorah hold its own against a who's who of kaiju, eventually succumbing to the combined might of Godzilla, Minilla, Mothra, Rodan, Manda, Gorosaurus, Anguirus, Kumonga, Baragon, and Varan. Even with three gravity-beam-blasting heads, that is hardly fair! Ghidorah returned with some backup for a final time in the Shōwa era in 1975's Godzilla vs. Gigan. This time, Ghidorah and his tag-team partner Gigan (who resembled a giant one-eyed space chicken) were under the control of cockroach-like Nebulans. Getting mind-controlled three times is just embarrassing! Fortunately, the Shōwa era drew to a close in 1975 before Ghidorah was forced into servitude for a fourth time. Mecha-King Ghidorah battling Godzilla in Godzilla Vs. King Ghidorah (1991). (Image credit: Tohu Pictures) Ghidorah returned in the rebooted Godzilla timeline of the Heisei era (1991–1998) in 1991's Godzilla Vs. King Ghidorah, but its cosmic origins are gone. The Heisei Ghidorah begins life as three genetically engineered creatures called Dorats in the future before being morphed into a three-headed form via nuclear exposure. Ghidorah was given a spiritual origin in the Millennium era's Godzilla, Mothra, and King Ghidorah: Giant Monsters All-Out Attack (2001), actually serving as a protagonist, helping Mothra in halting Godzilla's rampage. Ghidorah is once again an extraterrestrial in Universal Pictures' MonsterVerse movie Godzilla: King of the Monsters (2019), being described as having "fallen from the stars" in ancient times before rising to challenge Godzilla. Now King Ghidorah is back once again in Godzilla Minus Zero, maintaining his extraterrestrial origin story and once again challenging Godzilla to an epic kaiju battle. Those are some of the fictional versions of this golden beast, but what does it look like in reality? The real King Ghidorah! Arguably the most impressive feat of King Ghidorah has been to make itself such an important part of pop culture that astronomers took note. The King Ghidorah supercluster is a collection of galaxies located around 6.7 billion light-years from Earth. Covering an area of the sky equivalent to 19 full moons, as seen from our vantage point, this cosmic Kaiju was discovered in late 2022 by Japanese astronomers using data from the Subaru Telescope . A color composite image of the King Ghidorah supercluster was captured by the Subaru Telescope's prime focus camera (Image credit: NAOJ) The King Ghidorah supercluster is comprised of at least 19 individual associated galaxy clusters. It stretches out for an incredible 1.3 billion light-years, meaning the entire Milky Way could fit across it around 12,300 times. That makes it the largest supercluster ever discovered. To put into context just how monstrous the King Ghidorah supercluster is, consider the fact that it has a mass equivalent to 10,000,000,000,000,000 suns, 10 times as massive as the Milky Way's home supercluster, Laniakea . Even Godzilla may think twice before attempting to tussle with that particular King Ghidorah! See King Ghidorah in action in Godzilla Minus Zero, which is showing in theaters in the US and UK from November 6. You can see the preceding movie, Godzilla Minus One, on Netflix. item.title: Physicists listened to electrical noise to crack a superconductor mystery
item.description: Superconductors carry electricity without resistance, but most only work a few degrees above absolute zero. In the late 1980s, copper-based materials called cuprates were found to superconduct at higher temperatures—reachable with affordable liquid nitrogen. Yet nearly 40 years later, physicists still don't agree on why. In a recent Science study, a team of physicists led by Milan Allan of Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich and Ingmar Swart of Utrecht University in the Netherlands has found some answers by listening to the faint electrical crackle of current flowing into a cuprate. The missing electrons Central to the mystery of cuprates’ high-temperature superconductivity is a strange state called the pseudogap. “The pseudogap is a phenomenon of missing electrons,” Allan said. Above the temperature at which cuprates become superconducting, some of their electrons seem to vanish—measurements find far fewer of them at the energies where they should be. “Everybody knows that from different probes, you see that there's these vanishing electrons, but nobody knows why,” Allan said. Read full article Comments

item.title: Doom delivers five minutes of terminal violence on an IBM mainframe
item.description: Can an IBM Z mainframe run Doom? Of course it can. The more interesting question is whether you can play it through a text terminal without ruining your eyesight. WND Software's browser demo connects to an IBM Z mainframe over SSH using its terminal emulator. Wojciech Graj's DOOM-ASCII supplies the text-based carnage, replacing conventional graphics with colored characters. There's no sound. It is, however, completely playable (although you might need to recalibrate your vision to work out what is going on, particularly with regard to distant objects). Sessions are limited to five minutes, with room for up to 50 simultaneous users, but we had no trouble getting in. ASCII also presented no issues once the game was in motion. This writer played the original shareware release on an Amstrad ALT386SX portable, so squinting at an indistinct demon felt reassuringly familiar. That Doom can be persuaded to run on an IBM Z mainframe is not particularly noteworthy. The code has turned up everywhere from databases to PCB designers . Even the humble Pi Pico was roped into the fun. Keeping the action playable through a text terminal is the more entertaining achievement. A year ago, an IBM consultant persuaded Doom to run on IBM Z and LinuxONE using VNC to bring the pixelated mayhem to life. Using a terminal emulator, while a neat demonstration of the capabilities of WND's software, is perhaps more an example of "because I can" masochism. It's undeniably an enjoyable way to burn through five minutes. No installation or login required – just a willingness to shoot at punctuation. ®
